The filing also asserts that Uefa does not have the authority to initiate any criminal proceeding in Switzerland, as it is contractually bound by Fifa statutes to resolve any disputes with Fifa itself via arbitration.

Sports.title: ‘It’s huge’: Nike shirt deal breaks new ground for London City Lionesses
Sports.content:
The Women’s Super League club London City Lionesses’ new front-of-shirt sponsorship deal with Nike is the largest in the women’s game, according to their American owner, Michele Kang.

The length and value of the deal has not been disclosed but sources close to the WSL club are hailing it as a gamechanging moment and Kang claims that it even exceeds some men’s Premier League clubs’ shirt deals.

London City, who host Manchester United on Friday in the opening game of the new WSL campaign, are about to embark on only their second top-flight season, but this summer they have shocked the sport by signing a flurry of some of the biggest names in women’s football, including the former Ballon d’Or winner Alexia Putellas, the former England goalkeeper Mary Earps and Putellas’ Spain and Barcelona teammate, Mapi León.

It has been reported that the largest current front-of-shirt sponsorship deal for a women’s football team is an approximately $4m per year agreement reached by the new NWSL franchise in Atlanta – who will begin competing in 2028, but Kang told BBC Sport: “I can absolutely confirm that this is the largest women-only front-of-shirt deal. It is higher than the Atlanta number.

“I can absolutely also share that it is higher than some of the men’s Premier League front-of-shirt deals. It’s huge. That’s why it is landmark. There are so many other people who believe in the future of women’s football. They [Nike] didn’t make this decision lightly. They did not write a charity cheque. They believe in the future and they believe together we will invest and build this future together.”

View image in fullscreen Michele Kang has been London City Lionesses owner since December 2023. Photograph: Charlotte Wilson/Offside/Getty Images

The deal will be a major boost to London City’s finances. In their most recent set of financial accounts, they posted an annual revenue of just £902,000 for the 2024-25 season, when they won promotion to the top flight. Their operating loss was over £10m, and more than 10 times that revenue.

Their transfer business has attracted questions about how they can fit their lavish spending within the salary cap, as the WSL’s rules dictate that clubs cannot spend more on their player wage bills than 80% of their relevant revenue plus up to £4m of owner contributions. But it is understood this Nike deal will transform their annual revenue astronomically compared to previous seasons.

The popularity on social media of their biggest new signing Alexia Putellas – who has 3.4 million Instagram followers – and Earps and León is believed to have been a major driving factor in the supposedly high valuation from Nike. Putellas has helped Spain win 2023’s World Cup and won the Champions League four times with Barcelona. The Spaniard shared the news of the sponsorship on her Instagram account on Thursday.

Sports.title: Daniel Kretinsky to become biggest West Ham shareholder in blow to Amanda Staveley
Sports.content:
Daniel Kretinsky is set to become the biggest shareholder at West Ham after striking an agreement with David Sullivan, dealing a blow to Amanda Staveley’s hopes of buying a stake in the Championship club.

Staveley was a guest at the London Stadium for West Ham’s 4-2 win over Wolves earlier this week and was pushing to buy Vanessa Gold’s 25.1% stake in the club. The British businesswoman, previously a director at Newcastle, had struck a deal with the Gold family in July and was fronting a consortium looking for a way on to the east London club’s board.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

However that arrangement sparked a process allowing West Ham’s other shareholders to exercise their pre-emption rights over the Gold family’s stake before a 5.30pm deadline on Thursday evening. It is believed that Kretinsky, a Czech billionaire and the owner of Royal Mail, and Sullivan have come to an agreement that will see the former increase his 27% stake to 46%. Sources have said there is unlikely to be a way back for Staveley’s group.

Sources have consistently said that Kretinsky, who will surpass Sullivan as the biggest shareholder, is determined to increase his interest in West Ham as they look to rebuild after their relegation from the Premier League last season. His plans were complicated by Staveley entering the picture.

However it is understood that Sullivan rebuffed an inquiry from Staveley about buying his stake during the summer. The 77-year-old privately indicated a preference to deal with Kretinsky, who first bought a stake in West Ham in November 2021. The arrangement will see Sullivan increase his stake from 38.8% to 40%, making him the second largest shareholder. The American businessman Tripp Smith’s stake will go from 8% to 11% and the remaining shareholders will rise from 1.1% to 3%. Staveley would need shareholders not to take up their pre-emption rights to have a chance of making a separate offer for the Gold shares.

Sullivan stepped down as a director and co-chair of West Ham in June, before a joint investigation by the Times and Panorama reporting on seven women abusing his power and preying on them for sex in claims that date back to the 1980s and 90s. The 77-year-old categorically denies the allegations. Sullivan has been present at West Ham’s home games this season but does not have a seat on the board and is no longer the most powerful person at the club.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola defends Liverpool opting against throwing ‘crazy money’ at short-term fixes
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola has defended Liverpool’s summer transfer strategy and said the club were right not to pay “crazy money” for short-term fixes while Hugo Ekitiké, Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni are recovering from serious injuries.

Liverpool had the highest net spend in the Premier League, with Bradley Barcola, signed for a potential £123m, added on Monday to a front line that includes the £125m Alexander Isak and £116m Florian Wirtz. Barcola could make his debut at Ipswich on Friday, despite not featuring for Paris Saint-Germain this season.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Liverpool’s outlay did not include a right-back, defensive midfielder or right-winger but Iraola, who believes Barcola could be deployed in Mohamed Salah’s old position on the right, insisted he had no qualms with the squad at his disposal.

“I’m very happy with all the signings we’ve made,” said the Liverpool head coach. “I know the next question: ‘Do you want more signings in other positions?’ At the end the club has decided those signings we have done are the ones that improved our team and our position.

“There were other options we decided not to take, for different reasons: sometimes it is sporting reasons because they don’t improve what you have, sometimes it is economical reasons as it didn’t make sense in terms of the market to do those movements. But I’m happy now I know what we have, I have a lot of quality in the team and now it is the moment for us, for the players, for me to develop what we have.”

Leoni has been sidelined with an anterior cruciate ligament injury since last September but is expected to resume first-team training during the international break, which starts this month. There is no date on Bradley’s and Ekitiké’s return from serious knee and achilles injuries respectively, but Iraola said the club had to plan for the long term and wait for all three to recover.

Iraola said: “The club has decided not to sign someone because we need them for these two or three months and instead trust the players we have, us working with the players we have and thinking of the long term.

“Yes, as a manager you need the players for today but if they [the club] explain to you the vision and the long-term project, you also have to understand the club. Sometimes it doesn’t make sense to pay crazy money – the market was the market – for players who maybe in the long term you don’t need. Then you will need this money to solve other problems in that position. Sometimes it’s better to look a little bit further than the next game and the next month.”

Despite the absence of a natural right-winger – Liverpool explored deals for Yankuba Minteh at Brighton and Ismaïla Sarr at Crystal Palace – Iraola is confident Barcola, Victor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo and Rio Ngumoha will provide sufficient cover.

He said: “I think we’ve preferred at the end to have the best players, probably, than a player that maybe is specifically for that [right-sided] position. I’m very used from my previous teams to demand for all the wingers to play both sides.

“Probably all of them have played more on the left, but I would say I’ve seen them in a good place on the right. Probably Rio is more specific from the left side, but I think he has also showed the willingness to improve and play on the right. Even Bradley, he’s very open and I think he can play right and left. He started actually more on the right side when he started with Olympique Lyonnais. I’m happy with the four wingers we have and I’m sure we are going to be able to cover those two positions.”

Sports.title: Gabriel Martinelli leaves Arsenal for Saudi Arabian club Al-Hilal in £60m deal
Sports.content:
Arsenal have confirmed Gabriel Martinelli has joined the Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal for £60m. It is understood the deal for Brazil forward includes a sell-on clause.

Martinelli, who joined Arsenal from Ituano in 2019, has fallen down the pecking order at the Emirates despite being part of the squad that won the Premier League title last season. His fee surpasses the previous record £40m received by Arsenal when they sold Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain to Liverpool in 2017.

Quick Guide How do I 

Martinelli is believed to have signed a four-year contract worth about £17m a season. His move was widely expected after Arsenal agreed a deal last week and has gone through before the transfer window in Saudi Arabia closes on Sunday.

The 25-year-old joins his Brazil teammate Gabriel Jesus in leaving Arsenal this week, the striker having moved to Barcelona for £8.6m. The Premier League champions also sold Fábio Vieira to Hamburg on deadline day but decided against bringing in players.

Arsenal are believed to have received about £3m from Brook Norton-Cuffy’s £14m move from Genoa to Hull owing to a sell-on clause in the England Under-21 defender’s contract but missed out on about £7m when Folarin Balogun move to Everton collapsed.

Tottenham have omitted Richarlison from their Premier League squad, with the striker not a part of their plans for the season. They could have accommodated him for the first-half of the campaign because one of their 17 senior non-homegrown players – Xavi Simons – is out until March or April, according to the manager, Roberto Di Zerbi, with an anterior cruciate ligament injury.

Spurs made clear to Richarlison before the closure of the transfer window in England on Tuesday night that he would not be included so he could arrange a move. He was unable to do so, with one to his former club, Everton, not happening. He is the subject of firm interest from Trabzonspor in Turkey, where the window remains open until Friday night.

Richarlison posted a message on social media on Monday in which he said he would not allow anybody to decide his future for him. He talked about his commitment to Spurs; how “when everything here was falling apart and they needed me, I stayed and gave my life”.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Richarlison was Spurs’ top scorer in the league last season with 11 goals. He also said: “So I hope they treat my situation with the same respect that I’ve always had for the Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don’t try to decide for me.”

Sports.title: Naomi Osaka calls on US Open influencers to 'read up on tennis etiquette' after umpire was forced to tell off spectators during her first match
Sports.content:
Naomi Osaka called upon influencers travelling to the US Open to 'read up' on the sport's rules for spectators after her first-round match was disrupted by a rowdy group in one of Arthur Ashe Stadium's luxury suites.

The four-time Grand Slam champion had been preparing to serve when the chair umpire told off the guests for appearing to stage an impromptu photoshoot, complete with portable lights.

'Guys, please, in the suite behind me, please thank you guys, please take your seat,' the chair umpire announced to the stadium, as the broadcast camera panned to a group milling freely within their prime seats, taking pictures and talking.

While Osaka was only half-focused on the specifics of the incident while immersed in defeating her opponent Anastasia Zakharova, discussing what happened on the tournament's showcourt two days later, she suggested that more could be done to ensure that players were not disturbed during matchplay.

'I think obviously, if you come to a sporting event, you have to respect the sport,' she said after her defeat of Katerina Siniakova, which took place on the same court. 'And I feel like it's common courtesy to read up on the sport, especially the etiquette.

'I feel like it could be a good thing for people to make the sport of tennis popular to their specific audience, but I think it has to be managed a lot better, especially in the situation like first-round match.

Naomi Osaka called for fans new to tennis to learn the sport's etiquette after her match was disrupted by influencers

'Overall I think there is huge positives,' she added, on the topic of influencers more generally. 'You want people to continue to grow the sport. I just think it has to be in a way that everyone knows the rules and the etiquette.'

Etiquette largely dictates that fans should save conversation and movement for changeovers or set breaks, when the players are at the chairs. But in 2024, the US Open switched to a policy of 'free fan movement', which allows spectators to move during points regardless of on-court action.

Of the incident itself, Osaka said that she had been more bothered by the noise inside the stadium during both her matches - a constant chatter which complements the endless movement - than the flash lights themselves.

'I was going to say today the umpire, she told everyone to be quiet more than I've ever heard an umpire tell a crowd to be quiet,' she continued.

'I do think in my first match, I wasn't really paying attention. I tell people I normally just focus on the match and the court, but there was a moment where there was, like, people shouting, and you could hear it quite clearly. I think it bothered my opponent, too.

'Maybe that's what you were talking about, but I've heard some people say, like, the lights or whatever. I don't really see the lights, because obviously, when you are serving, you're looking at the sun or you're looking at the night lights. It was more the noise.'

Daily Mail Sport contacted the tournament for comment on after Osaka's press conference, with US Open head of communications Brendan McIntyre sharing the following statement: 'The USTA is always striving to grow tennis in this country and bring new audiences into the sport. The US Open is our greatest opportunity to do so, and we welcome newcomers to our event.

'We want all of our fans and guests to have an incredible time when they attend, but we also need to ensure they do not interfere with the action and competition on the court. We are continually looking for ways to ensure fans in the stands know what is permitted and what is prohibited.

'As a result, we have increased signage on the grounds and in stadium, and messaged ticket and suite holders to remind everyone to refrain from any activity that could disrupt the game, including noise levels, flash photography and ring lights. The chair umpire also has the ability to address the crowd if and when necessary.'

Sports.title: Last British star standing at the US Open Francesca Jones is downed by teen talent Iva Jovic - as all nine players fail to make the third round
Sports.content:
Last British star standing at the US Open Francesca Jones is downed by teen talent Iva Jovic - as all nine players fail to make the third round

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Britain's singles hopes at the US Open officially ended on Thursday evening, as Francesca Jones was knocked out in a gritty battle against rising American talent Iva Jovic, 6-4, 6-4.

Jones was the last Briton standing by virtue of the scheduling, the final match on Court 17 - the so-called 'weed court' - where she has previously played a number of qualifying matches. And in the first set, Jones put up more than enough fight to spare the blushes of her compatriots in the second round of the women's draw, Katie Boulter and Harriet Dart, who managed just five games between them in their straight-sets losses.

When Jovic grabbed the opening break, Jones' support may have feared the worst. The 18-year-old is already the 14th seed in Flushing Meadows, and has a fluid game style built on soaking up pressure and firing back bullets that may one day see her snap up the No1 seeding here.

After a run of three games, Jones stopped the rot with a break of Jovic's serve, and the match really began.

Jones is nothing if not a fighter. Describing how 'Northern grit' got her over the line in her stop-start, weather-disturbed win against Magda Linette, that was on full display here as she grew into the game in front of a partisan home crowd, her feel for the ball improving quickly in the early stages.

Jovic was put under pressure even in the games she won, with Jones frequently dogging her to deuce and keeping her foot on her opponent's serve. The opening set stretched to 56 minutes. Just three minutes shy of Boulter's entire star-crossed match against Karolina Muchova on Thursday.

Francesca Jones was unable to get past rising American star Iva Jovic on a tough evening

The 18-year-old is the 14th seed in Flushing Meadows but did not have an easy time against the British qualifier

The 25-year-old was able to hang tough in the rallies as she threw the book at Jovic, a variety of backhand slices splintering cross-court, deeply struck forehands, and the occasional net rush.

But there was a mental game to be played here. 'Confidence, it's all about confidence,' Jones' coach told her in Spanish, almost a mother tongue since her move to Barcelona to train at the age of nine. With Jovic reaching deuce looking to pull off yet another break for 5-3, Jones listened, knuckled down, and pulled off the all-important hold.

When Jovic's class told to hand her the opening set, it looked for a moment as if Jones' race was run. Four games on the run were gobbled up by Jovic, her spot in the third round almost in touching distance. But the Briton stayed cool, and continued to construct her points well. Suddenly, she had three break-point opportunities. One and two came and went, but as Jones wafted a sky-high moonball over to Jovic, she blinked, and fumbled her shot into the net. Finally, a game on the board. All about confidence? Jones sent some racquets off for re-stringing. That can take about 20 minutes. She was digging in.

As in the first set, Jovic looked to wrestle momentum back at 4-2. Again, Jones was in no mood to roll over. A wicked backhand ladened with unpredictable spin was too much for Jovic, and pulled back one break point, and three deuces eventually handed the hold to Jones a second time.

But Jovic chose a good time to serve well, and fast. For the first time since the very start of the match, the teenager was efficient in her hold. The conditions were steamy even as the clock ticked towards 9pm, and off-court relief beckoned. But as she looked to break Jones, her rival's dangerous slice again held back the tide, mulching two match-point opportunities for Jovic and allowing her to carry off a gutsy hold. With sweat pouring off both of the players, ball kids used the break to mop the court.

Jovic would have to do it on her own racquet, and with nerveless cool, shrugged off the late drama of a missed net cord to serve out the match. Her win in straight sets undersells how hard she had to fight against a player in Jones who won her first ever US Open main draw match on Wednesday.

British No2 - and onetime world No8 - Cameron Norrie was the first Briton with direct entry into the main draw to fall on the opening day's play, with defeat to French 22-year-old Luca van Assche.

Other first-round casualties included Arthur Fery, who lost in straight sets to Lorenzo Musetti, and Jan Choinski, who was despatched by the same scoreline to Botic van de Zandschulp. Qualifier Harry Wendelken was unable to see his strong form which gained him entry into the tournament proper translate against the No21 seed Luciano Darderi.

But fellow qualifiers Toby Samuel and Jacob Fearnley fared a little better, reaching the second round. Samuel put in a particularly bold performance against Tomas Machac, feasting on the inconsistent Czech to take him in straight sets. Fearnley meanwhile qualified as a lucky loser, and proved why he deserved his spot with an extended, heavily rain-delayed first-round victory against Martin Landaluce.

Both however fell in the second-round, with Samuel another victim of a challenging draw against Jiri Lehecka, and Fearnley leaving a fightback in the third set too late to make it stick against Tomas Martin Etcheverry. All three British women in the draw, Dart, Jones, and Boulter, made it to the second round.

Sports.title: Why Roberto De Zerbi still thinks he can get the best out of 'future Ballon d'Or winner' Mykhailo Mudryk at Tottenham, from their Shakhtar secrets to the 'hope' of Spurs' forward line
Sports.content:
Why Roberto De Zerbi still thinks he can get the best out of 'future Ballon d'Or winner' Mykhailo Mudryk at Tottenham, from their Shakhtar secrets to the 'hope' of Spurs' forward line

Tottenham's latest great hope is that Roberto De Zerbi will work some magic on Mykhailo Mudryk.

De Zerbi once hailed Mudryk as a future Ballon D'Or winner and sure enough the footage from a time when he was Brighton boss has resurfaced since the pair were reunited at Spurs on transfer deadline day.

They worked together at Shakhtar Donetsk, so De Zerbi has a good appreciation of the 25-year-old Ukraine who has joined him on loan for the season with a £75million option to buy.

He knows the depth of the winger's talent, his footballing strengths and weaknesses, his personality and attitude.

Unfortunately, much has gone awry for Mudryk since leaving Shakhtar.

His £89m move to Chelsea already looked like a flop when the doping ban hit in November 2024.

Mykhailo Mudryk has not played since November 2024, serving a year and a half of his four-year doping ban before it was cut short this summer

Mudryk and Roberto De Zerbi have reunited at Tottenham having worked together at Shakhtar Donetsk in the Ukraine

Now, two years after his last Premier League start, De Zerbi has set about the task of rekindling this talent and replenishing his morale in the hope it might solve a problem for Spurs.

It seems like a longshot and yet Mudryk is not the only great hope in play in N17.

Everyone hopes Dejan Kulusevski is nearing the end of his injury nightmare and will soon be back in contention. The same can be said for James Maddison and Mohamed Kudus, two of the most creative players at Spurs who hardly kicked a ball in 2026.

And for Dominic Solanke, whose last season was disrupted by injuries and who has missed part of pre-season with more niggling and unexplained issues.

Savio and Omar Marmoush have been lured from Manchester City's bench in the hope they might recapture form they showed before moving to English football.

Mathys Tel remains an enigma 20 months after his arrival from Bayern Munich but is only 21, still young, a work in progress and everyone hopes he can fulfil his vast potential.

De Zerbi's entire strike-force is built on hope.

Last night, Spurs confirmed their 25-man squad for the Premier League did not include Richarlison, the storm-tossed Brazilian now angling after a move to Trabzonspor before the Turkish transfer deadline on Friday.

Mudryk won player of the season in his one year under De Zerbi in 2021-22

His form for Shakhtar earned him his £89m move to Chelsea in January 2023

Richarlison was the top scorer for Spurs last season, and for all his faults, his omission leaves the attacking unit dangerously low on game time in recent months.

Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert are in the squad but weeks from fitness after serious knee injuries earlier this year and the other eight attacking or creative players total only 33 appearances and nine goals in the league this year.

There is never any such thing as a guarantee, but it feels like De Zerbi is taking off into the new season on a wing and a prayer when it comes to goals and an attacking threat.

Goals have been a problem ever since Ange Postecoglou's lust for thrills was replaced by Thomas Frank's caution and defensive security which cost the team fluency and sparked an over-reliance on goals from set pieces.

Since Frank was sacked, the threat from set pieces has faded and Spurs sold or released many of their strongest players in the air. Cristian Romero, Kevin Danso, Radu Dragusin, Joao Palhinha and Randal Kolo Muani have all departed.

Brentford tormented Spurs in the air on the opening day of the season. Others will take note.

Spurs' defensive upgrade made sense. It was complete in good time, early in the summer and injected much-needed leadership, experience and proven Premier League quality into the squad.

Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes were expensive and are yet to find their best rhythm but should strengthen midfield.

Questions linger about Toni Kinsky as the number one goalkeeper, but when Cody Gakpo and Iliman Ndiaye escaped Spurs, it left uncertainty swirling around firepower.

De Zerbi's team are one of three Premier League teams without a goal from the opening two games.

Mudryk's career is at a crossroads and he desperately needs to revive his fortunes at Spurs

Still, there's always hope.

Marmoush was red hot for 18 months at Eintracht Frankfurt. Savio had that good year at Girona and dazzled on his debut against Charlton's reserves in the Carabao Cup only to miss the Newcastle defeat because Spurs physios detected muscle fatigue.

This is always a concern for those who are not conditioned by the rigours of regular competitive football.

Nobody expects Kulusevski will return in the same sublime form he was in under Postecoglou two years ago. Nobody would be surprised if he encountered a physical setback or two as he returned.

The same is true for Maddison, who for various reasons has not started a game for even longer than Kulusevski. And for Kudus, who has not started a game since January.

Mudryk has not been injured but has been out for the longest of all.

The relationship at Shakhtar counts for something, but it is a very tall order to expect De Zerbi to bring him back to the boil instantly.

Much of the excitement about Mudryk's potential resides in a six-week spell when he scored eight in 10 games for Shakhtar, a flurry that sparked a rush for his signature, led by Arsenal for a long time and won by Chelsea who gave him an eight-and-a-half-year contract.

De Zerbi had left Ukraine by this stage. Having arrived at Shakhtar at the start of the season which never returned from its winter break because of Russia invading in February 2022, the Italian quit and was out of work until Brighton appointed him in September 2022.

He did give Mudryk his big break however, and the young winger responded.

Enzo Maresca was in charge of Chelsea when Mudryk returned the positive result for banned the substance meldonium in October 2024

'I know the value of Mudryk,' said De Zerbi when Brighton boss and Premier League clubs were chasing the Shakhtar winger. 'He can win the Ballon D'Or in future. He has the quality to become a star.'

Mudryk's exhilarating speed is his key asset, and he delivered many of his most exciting Shakhtar performances in the surreal environment of wartime football played at neutral venues behind closed doors.

Upon joining Chelsea in January 2023, he went 10 months without a goal.

He flickered without convincing amid the managerial whirl at Stamford Bridge from Graham Potter to Frank Lampard to Mauricio Pochettino and Enzo Maresca, who was in charge when he returned the positive result for the banned substance meldonium during an out-of-competition test while training with Ukraine in October 2024.

None of them denied he had genuine talent. None though could translate it to the Premier League.

By the time of the ban, Mudryk was firmly on the outskirts of Maresca's team. His last three Chelsea goals were scored in the early rounds of what became a procession to the Europa Conference League.

In the Premier League under Maresca, he had been reduced to the role of a late substitute whose extreme pace might cause problems for tired defenders when the game was stretched open and misshapen near the end.

So, there is more to rehabilitating Mudryk than simply making up for time missed, he must also reach a level that seemed beyond him before the ban.

If he has an impact at Spurs it will be for the first time in English football and it will one way or another benefit their bitter London rivals Chelsea.

Perhaps it is a sign of De Zerbi's desperation that he thinks it is worth a shot.

At least, with no European competition there is the time to work on the training pitch, drilling shape and searching of his best formula and should not need to overload those who are so short of competitive football.

Fingers crossed Spurs fans.

Sports.title: Federico Chiesa is left OUT of Liverpool's 25-man Champions League squad in latest blow to Italian - as three injured stars and youngster with only three Premier League appearances make the cut instead
Sports.content:
Federico Chiesa is left OUT of Liverpool's 25-man Champions League squad in latest blow to Italian - as three injured stars and youngster with only three Premier League appearances make the cut instead

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Federico Chiesa's Liverpool career has taken another hit after he was omitted from their UEFA Champions League squad.

The Reds have submitted their 25-man squad for Europe's elite club competition which begins on Tuesday.

Liverpool begin their quest for an seventh European Cup when they face Atletico Madrid at Anfield on Wednesday night.

However, Chiesa will play no part in the tournament after new boss Andoni Iraola chose to not include him for their European campaign. Wataru Endo is another.

Chiesa has missed the Merseyside outfit's first two Premier League games of the season due to a muscle injury but when fit will find himself further down their pecking order following the summer signings of fellow forwards Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz.

And it is a case of deja-vu for Chiesa, who suffered the same fate from Iraola's predecessor Arne Slot. However, Chiesa was later called-up for their 25-man squad after centre back Giovanni Leoni tore his anterior cruciate ligament.

Leoni is one of three Liverpool players currently out injured though that have been selected by Iraola - with Conor Bradley and Hugo Ekitike completing the trio.

Federico Chiesa has been omitted from Liverpool's 25-man squad for the Champions League

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola (left) has selected Hugo Ekitike though despite his achilles injury

Leoni is set to return to training later this month after nearly a year out, Bradley has been out of action since suffering a knee injury in January and Ekitike has been sidelined since tearing his achilles in April.

The inclusion of the injured trio gives Liverpool fans encouragement that they will be involved before the conclusion of the league phase on January 27, 2027.

Endo, who like Chiesa has not featured in the opening two matches of the season, has been omitted with James McConnell, 21, preferred among the midfielders.

Fellow academy graduates Luke Chambers and Isaac Mabaya are named among 11 defenders on the list.

Under UEFA rules, the 25 players named in List A has to include a minimum of eight ‘locally trained’ squad members. Youngsters such as Rio Ngumoha and Trey Nyoni aren’t among them as they can be named on List B given their age. That won't change until they turn 21.

Sports.title: How influencers are killing the US Open and turning it into a 'zoo': Angry top stars hit out at 'disrespectful' and noisy content creators disrupting matches for pictures
Sports.content:
How influencers are killing the US Open and turning it into a 'zoo': Angry top stars hit out at 'disrespectful' and noisy content creators disrupting matches for pictures

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Naomi Osaka was not having the easiest time on court. Having battled through a tie-break to edge the first set, she was serving at 4-4 in the second. Then, her concentration snapped.

Up in the luxury suites, a group of influencers were posing for photographs using a bright, portable light. As they milled about the box, unaware of the tension below, their distraction was enough to prompt a warning from the chair umpire. But it took a few moments for the message to filter through. After all, their focus was on getting the perfect shot.

Welcome to the 2026 US Open. Long the envy of the Grand Slams for the late-night energy and glamour that only New York can provide, this year's tournament has been subject to complaints about being overrun with influencers who see the final major of the year as little more than a creative backdrop on social media.

'People are down there trying to perform, and it's their career and their job. It seems like a bit disrespectful,' US No 1 Jessica Pegula said when asked about the incident in Osaka's match after her own bow on Arthur Ashe, the tournament's biggest court. 'I think it's gotten a little too much, it feels, this year.'

There's no mystery behind why the US Open has become such a popular destination to tick off for the well-travelled influencer.

'The US Open has evolved from a tennis tournament into one of the most powerful cultural points on the New York calendar,' notes Reece Milner, Senior Strategy Manager at The Goat Agency, a creator and influencer marketing shop. 'It now sits at the intersection of sport, fashion, luxury, hospitality, celebrity, lifestyle and content culture.'

The 'rituals' that appear so frequently on social media feeds that you might be able to play US Open bingo, like enjoying a night match, a Honey Deuce cocktail or $100 COQODAQ chicken nugget-and-caviar box, Milner adds, have only served to crystallise its status.

A group of influencers caught flack for using a portable light to take pictures during Naomi Osaka's match

The US Open has seen a huge rise in popularity in recent years and brands hosting influencers at the tournament in a bid to borrow its cultural clout has risen too

This is no one-way street either, with the US Open well aware of its cultural power outside of tennis as well as within. The tournament has embraced the influencer, this year going as far as to credential 100 content creators, with US Open head of communications Brendan McIntyre noting that in years to come, the number is only going to 'go upwards'.

But those influencers aren't necessarily the problem. Tennis media has evolved to take in TikTok, Instagram, and Substack experts, all invested in growing interest in the game itself. More worthy of skepticism are those who might be spending one night at the Open, making it a race against time to get the perfect picture, action on court be damned.

The US Open has never been Wimbledon, and that's a good thing. The noise of an Arthur Ashe night session makes for pleasing whiplash after the prim-and-proper hush of Centre Court as the tour bounces between the two majors.

But as greater numbers of guests flood into the Billie Jean King National Tennis Center with limited interest in the tennis and more on their feed, the noise levels of ambient chatter, rather than engagement in the match, have caused problems for players.

'On Ashe, you hear everything,' Pegula added. 'Even when there's dead noise, there's still a buzz or a chatter or people talking and eating and laughing and all these different kind of emotions. You really have to do a good job of locking yourself in a bubble when you're out there.'

Of fans on the outdoor courts, French player Adrian Mannarino was more forthright: 'They come in any which way, they move around, they talk. It's the tournament that tolerates this, and I don't know if it's the best idea for the game in general. There's noise coming from everywhere. It's become a bit of a zoo.'

Watching Aryna Sabalenka and Carlos Alcaraz on Arthur Ashe on Wednesday, the noise of the crowd never dipped below 'pub garden'. Since the tournament ushered in 'free fan movement' in 2024 which allows fans to come and go without waiting for changeovers or set breaks, the policy has been followed to the letter, with the lower bowl constantly in motion.

Influencers have added to the heat around the US Open and their enviable photographs will have translated, in part, to ticket sales

Inside Arthur Ashe Stadium is a constant hum of noise as fans move in their seats during points

That's where most of the chatter comes from too, with the seats in the gods crammed with fans locked in on the action, and quieter during play.

As Alcaraz took the first game after losing his opening set to Jaime Faria, the noise rises to a roar, with the same staticky thickness of a sound machine playing a recording of the ocean at full volume. At 0-15, clearly distracted, the Portuguese player serves a double fault. The chair umpire gives a warning when a fan shouts down from the stands as he's preparing to serve again, but does little to dim the constant conversation.

Nor have those in the suites learned their lesson. Despite the US Open displaying messages around the site telling fans to refrain from using flash or lights to take pictures, Daily Mail Sport spotted flashes going off during Sabalenka's thrashing of Polina Iatcenko.

A statement shared after the Osaka incident placed the responsibility for wrangling misbehaving influencers on the chair umpires, who 'have the ability to address the crowd' when 'infrequent' disruptions occur. On Thursday, an extended second statement responding to Osaka's comments added that the tournament has 'increased signage on the grounds and in stadium, and messaged ticket and suite holders to remind everyone to refrain from any activity that could disrupt the game, including noise levels, flash photography and ring lights.'

Influencers have added to the heat around the US Open and their enviable photographs will have translated, in part, to ticket sales. But if the goal is to get more fans into the sport, week-in, week-out, they need great tennis played in a great tennis atmosphere - and inside on the tournament's biggest courts, that can no longer be guaranteed.

Sports.title: FIFA accuse UEFA of a 'smear campaign' against Gianni Infantino and Co after European body threatened legal action as war over failed World Cup sell-off plans escalates
Sports.content:
FIFA says legal applications made by UEFA to access documents related to FIFA's controversial private investor plan are part of a 'smear campaign' against the global governing body. UEFA is applying through the American courts for discovery of evidence and documentation linked to FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a private company which it was envisaged would run the World Cup and other FIFA competitions. FIFA confirmed last month the plan had been to sell a 20 per cent stake in that company to private investors. The plan was withdrawn by FIFA president Gianni Infantino on August 1 amid opposition from UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and CONCACAF, the confederation for countries in North and Central America plus the Caribbean. That withdrawal has not stopped UEFA pursuing Infantino and other FIFA officials, with UEFA saying documents obtained were intended for use in preparing potential criminal proceedings in Switzerland, in filings seen by the Press Association on August 27. The following day, FIFA sought approval to oppose UEFA's request in the Southern District of Florida, a motion which was granted by the court on the next business day, August 31. FIFA has until September 28 to submit a full opposition to that court. A similar motion to oppose was also filed in the Southern District of New York on Tuesday. Documents from FIFA's legal team seen by the Press Association describe UEFA's applications as being 'little more than press releases in further support of UEFA's smear campaign against FIFA and its leadership'. UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin (left) and FIFA counterpart Gianni Infantino are at loggerheads over the latter's failed proposals for World Cup private investor plans FIFA's filing asks the New York court to defer consideration on UEFA's discovery application until the Florida court has ruled on it, or requests that the court permit FIFA permission to oppose UEFA's application no later than September 30. The filing said UEFA's motivation in its opposition to FFE and Infantino was 'to prevent smaller countries from having the financial strength to compete with the European elite'. It added: 'If soccer is strengthened in the developing world, global competition increases, which ultimately reduces UEFA's market power and provides more competition for its flagship tournaments. 'By raising funds to allow some of FIFA's smaller member associations to better develop soccer, FFE would lead to more players from those nations choosing to represent their countries of origin and playing in their home leagues rather than playing abroad. 'All of this would erode UEFA's dominance over other regions of the world.' UEFA's filing accused Infantino of 'criminal mismanagement' in relation to FFE, and said the proposed sale of a stake for £3.1billion ($4.2bn) in the company was 'a fraudulently off-market price promoted by Infantino for his own benefit'. In a separate statement published last week, UEFA called for an independent external review of the origins of the FFE and said that if Infantino chose to stand for re-election at next year's FIFA Congress, UEFA would 'join forces with its partner confederations to ensure that member associations are offered a credible alternative - one committed to integrity, accountability, development and genuine institutional change'.

Sports.title: Aston Villa handed major boost as new £60m star Johan Manzambi returns to training - but he may not be risked for Hull clash
Sports.content:
Johan Manzambi trained with his Aston Villa team-mates on Thursday fuelling hopes that his debut could arrive sooner than expected.

The club-record signing from Freiburg had a knee injury when he joined Villa in July in a deal worth up to £60million, and he has yet to play as he continues his recovery.

Yet Daily Mail Sport understands Manzambi took part in Thursday's session, though it is unclear at this stage whether he would be considered for Saturday's trip to Hull, where Villa will hope to claim their first points of the season after consecutive defeats to Brighton and Arsenal.

After the 1-0 home defeat by Arsenal on August 31, Emery was cautious about Manzambi, though he hoped the 20-year-old would be able to join in this week.

He said: 'We must be careful. He had an injury and we want his comeback to be clear and strong, with no risk.

'Progressively, he is working individually and is starting collectively with the group this week.'

Johan Manzambi trained with his Aston Villa team-mates on Thursday as he stepped up his recovery

After losing key members of the team who lifted the Europa League and qualified for the Champions League last term, Villa have tried to rebuild by making 11 signings. Emery has also brought forward Brian Madjo and midfielder George Hemmings into the first-team group.

Morgan Rogers moved to Chelsea this summer for a record £117m, with Emi Martinez also making the switch to Stamford Bridge. Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne, Ollie Watkins and Ezri Konsa also departed in a summer of huge change at Villa Park.

Sports.title: Roy Keane goes viral after leaving Gary Neville and Co in stitches with hilarious comparison between football stat and 'speaking to girls in a nightclub'
Sports.content:
Roy Keane left his Stick to Football colleagues in fits of laughter following his thoughts about the statistic 'Expected Goals' (xG). Speaking on the latest episode of the show, brought to you by Disney+, the former Manchester United captain expressed why he believes that particular stat - which measures the probability that a given shot will result in a goal - is irrelevant. Sitting alongside Gary Neville, Jamie Carragher, Jill Scott and Ian Wright, Keane started his point animatedly with: 'Do you know what that stat is? 'Years ago, when you'd go to a nightclub back in the day, and you'd chat to a girl all night, but you go home by yourself. What's your xG?' Keane's quip left Neville, Carragher, Scott and Wright in stitches. Neville then replied self-depreciatingly: 'Roy, I kept clean sheets!' A smirking Roy said: 'I'm sure you did, yeah!' xG explained the Roy Keane way! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/qJOS705noc — The Overlap (@WeAreTheOverlap) September 3, 2026 Roy Keane left his Stick to Football colleagues laughing with his views on Expected Goals (xG) Gary Neville (left) and Jamie Carragher were in hysterics after Keane compared it to nightclubs During the show, the quintet discussed the closing of the summer transfer window - following Tuesday's 11pm deadline. Among the clubs discussed was Liverpool - with Carragher believing Reds boss Andoni Iraola needs to have an awkward conversation with his vice-captain Dominik Szoboszlai and move him to right back permanently. Szoboszlai, 25, was rewarded with a new £350,000-a-week contract this summer after being named Liverpool’s Player of the Season for his impressive performances in midfield last campaign - one of the few positives in what was otherwise a disappointing season for the Reds under Arne Slot. Despite establishing himself as a mainstay in midfield, the Hungarian has also been called upon to deputise at right-back, doing so sporadically last season and again during the second half of Liverpool’s 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest on Saturday. Carragher believes Szoboszlai may be tasked with the right-back role permanently after Liverpool's disjointed start under Iraola, who has drawn both his Premier League matches so far. With Conor Bradley still injured and Jeremie Frimpong struggling for form, right-back has become a problem position for Liverpool since Trent Alexander-Arnold's exit to Real Madrid last summer. Fearing it was a 'massive mistake' not to bolster Liverpool's ranks at full back in the transfer window, Carragher is confident Szoboszlai could provide a solution for Iraola. Carragher believes Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola (right) needs to have an awkward conversation with his vice-captain Dominik Szoboszlai (left) and move him to right-back 'The big thing he (Iraola) has got, and it happened last season and at the weekend, Szoboszlai went back to right-back. I've never believed Szoboszlai is a central midfield player,' Carragher said. 'Now, he's signed a new contract and I can only imagine in those talks, they were desperate for him to stay, he's almost said "I want to play midfield". He's moved around a bit and he started the season in central midfield. I don't see him as that. 'For me, in midfield he's a Jordan Henderson. Runner, energy, with more of a goal threat. But Liverpool don't play that way and he's not really a No 10. His best role could actually be at right-back. He'd get plenty of the ball, he can run and almost play that Trent role from there. 'But there's no way he's going to want to play there because he's just signed a new contract for £350,000 a week. You've just done this big thing, he's the vice-captain, I just think that's a conversation Iraola is going to have to have going forward, because the midfield is not right and he's part of that midfield not being right.'

Sports.title: 'I joined Liverpool despite Real Madrid wanting me - but I regret how things panned out'
Sports.content:
'I joined Liverpool despite Real Madrid wanting me - but I regret how things panned out'

The ex-Liverpool star could have signed for Real Madrid just before he put pen to paper with the Reds

View 4 Images Liverpool signed Markus Babbel in 2000 (Image: EMPICS Sport)

Former Liverpool defender Markus Babbel previously opened up about his bittersweet spell at Anfield. The German star revealed that he had almost moved to Real Madrid ahead of the Reds and later regretted the way his time at Anfield ended.

‌



Liverpool signed Markus Babbel on a free transfer from Bayern Munich in the summer of 2000. Babbel helped Gerard Houllier’s side win a famous treble and qualify for the Champions League in 2000/01.

‌



The right-back was ever-present in the Premier League and started all 60 of his appearances, scoring six goals and bagging five assists. It could have been very different, however, for the now 53-year-old.

‌



“Yeah, yeah, Real Madrid wanted me,” he previously said when speaking to the Liverpool Echo on behalf of NewBettingSites.uk. “And it was a funny story because there was an agent there.

“He said: ‘Listen, tomorrow I will bring you a $1m if you're not going somewhere else, if you sign for Real Madrid. And I said: ‘Oh, thank you very much, but Real Madrid is not my club’.

Andoni Iraola gives update on Bradley Barcola and when he could make Liverpool debut READ MORE :

Liverpool considered 8 wingers in summer transfer window before landing Bradley Barcola READ MORE :

“If I go to Spain, then the only team I would sign for is Barcelona, because I am a massive Barcelona supporter and Real Madrid wasn't ever my club and my team. They have the best players, but this is not my club.

‌



“And, the funny thing is, I was on the way to Liverpool to sign the new contract. 6am in the morning and on the radio, the news came: ‘Spectacular, Markus Babbel is signing for Real Madrid! And I was on the way to Manchester, and driving over to Liverpool to sign the contract. That was a bit funny.”

Babbel started Liverpool’s Charity Shield and European Super Cup victories over Manchester United and Bayern the following August. Little did he know that his career on Merseyside was about to tragically unravel.

View 4 Images Markus Babbel became a cult hero on Merseyside (Image: Daily Mirror)

‌



Taken off at half-time in the Reds’ Premier League games with West Ham United and at Bolton Wanderers, out of breath, the full-back was diagnosed with the debilitating Guillain-Barre syndrome and was left in a wheelchair.

He battled back to fitness, returning in August 2002, but struggled to rediscover his previous form and fell out with Houllier. He was later sent off twice while playing for the reserves with the Reds' French boss later confirming that Babbel had no future at the club.

‌



Looking back, the German regrets how his Liverpool career ended. “Yeah (I have regrets) but this is part of my life now,” he admitted. “You know, of course, I was a bit sad because after this fantastic first season. I always say, okay, this illness happened, you know, I can't change it anymore. And it was a bad period.

“The only thing that I sometimes think, if this illness would come, a year later, you know, that I could play a second year for Liverpool. But it's happened, you know, and to be fair, after this illness, I wasn't the same person as before.

View 4 Images Gerard Houllier and Markus Babbel patched up their differences (Image: Getty)

‌



“I don't know, maybe in England, it's the same. In Germany. You say that the most important thing is the health, but you just say it, you know?

“But I was in a bad period, and I really was lying on the bed and I was thinking: ‘I give all my money back. I give all my titles back. The most important thing, I hope I get healthy again’.

“And, I had the luck to get past the bad illness. But I wasn’t the same person as before because I got divorced so my wife left England, my kids left England.

‌

“So I was alone there and something happened in my head. I wasn't normal anymore, you know, I went out a lot. I was drinking a lot. I wasn't professional anymore. My lifestyle didn't fix to a professional footballer. And, that was the reason why I had to leave this club. To go back to Germany first.”

Despite their falling out, Babbel revealed he had made peace with the late Liverpool manager. “Afterwards, the good thing for me was, the 25th Hillsborough anniversary, there was a game in Liverpool at Anfield,” he said. “I was invited as well. And Gerard Houllier was the manager.

‌



View 4 Images Markus Babbel opened up on his short career with Liverpool (Image: 2021 DeFodi Images)

“I went to him. I said: ‘Boss, I understand everything what you did. You were absolutely right. I was totally wrong. Sorry about this, but my head was lost. I was lost’.

“And so we had a good, good chat in this moment... But it is part of my life, you know. Of course I wish I could play a season, two seasons more for Liverpool. But, after this illness, I wasn't the same person anymore.”

Babbel would go on to spend the 2003/04 season on loan at Blackburn Rovers before joining VfB Stuttgart on a free transfer in the summer of 2004, and he remained there until 2007, where he retired from the game. Spells in management at the likes of Stuttgart, Hertha Berlin and Western Sydney Wanderers followed.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Cody Gakpo's future clear as star issues statement after late transfer drama
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Cody Gakpo's future clear as star issues statement after late transfer drama

The fallout from a chaotic deadline day in the transfer window continues for Liverpool

View 2 Images Cody Gakpo almost left Liverpool this summer (Image: 2025 Getty Images)

On Friday evening, Andoni Iraola will lead his Liverpool side into a Premier League game without the buzz of the transfer window hanging over him for the first time this season. Liverpool are looking for their first win of the new campaign, having drawn their opening two fixtures against Newcastle United and Nottingham Forest.

‌



Premier League new boys Ipswich Town, at Portman Road, are the challengers. While many fans will be eager to put transfers behind them for now and turn their attention to on-pitch matters, the fallout from the Reds' summer window continues regardless.

‌



One of the primary talking points over the last few months has been Cody Gakpo's proposed departure, with Tottenham and Manchester City registering their interest in the player. Another was the host of players leaving Anfield as the window sped to a conclusion.

‌



Today's news sees Iraola address Gakpo's current feelings after his cancelled transfer, while a departing star has made his thoughts clear on his Anfield exit.

Gakpo's future clear

Cody Gakpo appears undeterred and ready to go despite almost leaving Liverpool on deadline day. After being courted by Tottenham Hotspur for much of the summer, the Dutchman became a target for City, who were willing to pay around £85million for the 27-year-old forward.

Mo Salah jets back to Liverpool as wife gives birth to third child with name revealed READ MORE :

Andoni Iraola gives update on Bradley Barcola and when he could make Liverpool debut READ MORE :

The switch would only have materialised if Liverpool had brought in another attacker. But with moves for Crystal Palace's Isamaila Sarr and Brighton's Yankuna Minteh not forthcoming, Gakpo's exit was blocked as the Reds rejected City's bid.

‌



The Dutch star, who has started the season well, will be in the squad to face Ipswich. Iraola has claimed he has had an open dialogue with Gakpo throughout the transfer drama and is happy to pick him for the Premier League tie.

View 2 Images Cody Gakpo has a goal and an assist from the opening two games of the season (Image: Getty Images)

"My relationship with Cody has been very honest from the beginning," The Basque head coach said. "He has played very well for us so far. He was always aware of the situation in the market, we were constantly talking, I hope we can keep him at the same level. He is in a good place physically and mentally and I'm very happy to pick him."

‌

Liverpool signed Bajcetic in 2021 and he broke into the first team a year later and looked set to star in the midfield for years to come. However, a calf injury wrecked his development and forced him to miss most of the 2023/24 season. The 21‑year‑old then struggled in loan spells at Red Bull Salzburg and Las Palmas.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Having entered the final year of his contract at Anfield, Liverpool decided to sell Bajcetic for a profit rather than risk losing him for nothing next summer. The midfielder has no hard feelings, clearly.

Part of the Spanish star's message read: "The love you have gave me throughout the 5 years I spent in Liverpool has been incredible, it’s easy to show love when things go in the right direction, but as you know it hasn’t always been the case with me, and you have been there for me at all times.

‌



"This club is a massive family and it wouldn’t be with all the people that work for it, from chefs, kitchen staff, player care, groundskeepers, media, kit man, and all the hundred departments this club has, everyone makes out life so much easier and keeps this club as big as it is. I will miss you so much.

Sports.title: Arsenal could sign Barcelona star, wonderkid striker and free agent in transfers next year
Sports.content:
Arsenal could sign Barcelona star, wonderkid striker and free agent in transfers next year

Mikel Arteta could make some major additions to his Arsenal squad from as early as January

View 6 Images Mikel Arteta has some decisions to make (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Arsenal could improve their squad even further in just a few months after spending almost £200million this summer. Mikel Arteta added more firepower to his midfield and defence by securing Bruno Guimaraes, Ezri Konsa and Piero Hincapie.

‌



Christos Tzolis was the only attacking signing made by the Gunners after he joined from Club Brugge. Arteta had urged the club to "make some very important decisions" during the window but they failed to secure a marquee forward addition.

‌



Arsenal did make attempts for Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez and Vinicius Jr from Real Madrid but they failed to materialise. The club also sold Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and allowed Gabriel Martinelli to depart for Al-Hilal in a deal worth £60m.

‌



Viktor Gyokeres, Kai Havertz, Max Dowman, Noni Madueke, Eberechi Eze and Bukayo Saka are still on the Gunners' books this season. But if the club struggles in attack in the near future, then Arteta could make some exciting moves to add to his squad.

Arsenal medical underway with third Gunners signing already lined up for 2027 READ MORE :

Here, Mirror Football have looked at five players Arsenal could sign in the next couple of windows.

Julian Alvarez

The transfer saga concluded with Alvarez staying put at Atletico Madrid. Despite the Argentina international reportedly favouring a switch to Barcelona, the forward's decision could shift over the coming months.

‌



View 6 Images Arsenal did move for Julian Alvarez (Image: Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Should Arsenal manage to secure Alvarez, the 26-year-old could be a major coup for the club's attack.

Eli Junior Kroupi

Bournemouth were resolute that Kroupi would not be departing this summer, and their position was strengthened by the 20-year-old's recovery from injury. The gifted forward drew widespread interest after scoring 13 league goals for the Cherries last season and Arsenal reportedly maintained an interest in Kroupi prior to the summer transfer window.

‌



View 6 Images The Gunners were also keen on Eli Junior Kroupi (Image: Robin Jones - AFC Bournemouth/AFC Bournemouth via Getty Images)

The Independent reports that Kroupi will "almost certainly" be an option the Gunners revisit in January. Signing him would substantially strengthen Arteta's choices, both immediately and for the future, with Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres vying to be the club's leading striker.

Andreas Schjelderup

Should Arsenal be willing to wait until next summer for a new left-winger, Benfica star Andreas Schjelderup could turn out to be a steal. New signing Tzolis will only have Eze for competition on the left flank after the Gunners decided to cash in on multiple forwards this summer.

‌



View 6 Images Andreas Schjelderup has bags of potential (Image: Maciej Rogowski/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images)

Schjelderup's contract runs until 2028, meaning the Norway international will enter the final 12 months of his deal next summer, potentially resulting in a reduced transfer fee. The 22-year-old is a promising talent with considerable scope for development.

Raphinha

A left-winger who would provide Arsenal with an immediate solution out wide. The 29-year-old is the Barcelona captain but will be in the final year of his contract next summer.

‌



View 6 Images Raphinha could be convinced to return to England (Image: Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

The Brazilian boasts extraordinary talent, having netted 80 goals and laid on 60 assists in 180 appearances for the Catalan club. Bringing Raphinha to the Emirates would also allow Arsenal to harness his wealth of experience and winning mentality.

Karou Mitoma

Arsenal could replicate their Leandro Trossard masterstroke by swooping for Karou Mitoma as an established Premier League performer from Brighton.

‌



View 6 Images Kaoru Mitoma would be a smart signing (Image: Sebastian Frej/MB Media/Getty Images)

While not a long-term solution, the 29-year-old is entering the final year of his contract and could thrive within Arsenal's setup, either as a cut-price January signing or on a free transfer next summer.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua driver was 'attempting to overtake' when car crashed killing his two pals
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua driver was 'attempting to overtake' when car crashed killing his two pals

Adeniyi Mobolaji Kayode was driving the vehicle in Nigeria when two of Anthony Joshua's friends were killed in a car crash and has been accused of causing death by dangerous driving

View 2 Images Adeniyi Mobolaji Kayode is accused of causing death by dangerous driving (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The driver who was behind the wheel of the car carrying Anthony Joshua when it crashed killing two of the boxer's friends was attempting to overtake another vehicle at the time of the tragedy, a court has heard.

Adeniyi Mobolaji Kayode, 46, has been accused of causing death by dangerous driving and driving without a valid license. He denies the charges.

Joshua's personal trainer Latif Ayodele and strength coach Sina Ghami were both killed in the collision. Joshua and his pals were travelling to see his dad in Ogun, near Lagos, and are said to have been sleeping at the time of the incident.

A court heard Kayode lost control of the vehicle, a Lexus, and has been accused of trying to overtake a moving truck when he crashed into a parked lorry.

Tyson Fury provides Anthony Joshua fight update with talks on brink of collapse READ MORE :

Joshua, 36, was rushed to hospital following the crash on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway in Makun. The driver of the parked lorry the car careered into, Abubaka Adamu, 35, has denied a charge of obstructing the free flow of traffic.

Speaking in court, Inspector Christopher Ajayi Taiwo of the Ogun State Motor Traffic Division said both vehicles had been removed by the time he arrived at the scene.

Article continues below

He added that painkillers, an energy drink and a logbook were recovered near the driver's side at the site of the crash. The court also heard that local police had yet to take a statement from Joshua.

Kayode's lawyer asked Ajayi why that had not happened, to which he replied he 'didn't have his number'. The trial has been adjourned until September 10.

View 2 Images Anthony Joshua (C) with Latif Ayodele (L) and Sina Ghami (R)

Article continues below

The crash occurred in December 2025, just 10 days after Joshua had beat YouTuber Jake Paul in devastating fashion. Joshua returned to action against Kristian Penga in July, breaking down in tears as he paid tribute to his friends after the fight.

“I don’t want to talk about it anymore," he said. Joshua wore the names of his pals on pendants pinned to his chest as he took to the ring before the fight. He also had 'LATZ' and 'SINA' tattooed on his bicep.

Joshua is in negotiations to finally fight long-time British heavyweight rival Tyson Fury in November, but disagreements over the venue have put the mega bout at risk.

Sports.title: Mike Dean 'nonsense' claims rubbished by former referees as FA urged to investigate
Sports.content:
Mike Dean 'nonsense' claims rubbished by former referees as FA urged to investigate

Controversial retired official Mike Dean's comments about his time as a Premier League referee has led to a strong reaction from two former top-flight officials

View 2 Images Mike Dean (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire)

Two former Premier League referees have criticised Mike Dean after the ex-official claimed to have played secret ‘games’ in matches during his time in the top flight. The former referee claimed that such games would involve waiting to see how long he could go without blowing the whistle or leaving the centre circle.

‌



Dean spent more than two decades as a referee in English football before retiring from the profession in 2022, and went on to spend a further year as a video assistant referee.

‌



During an appearance on Jamie Vardy's Having a Party podcast, Dean said: "There used to be games that we used to have, as a laugh, we used to say, 'Right, we'll kick off now, right? See how long we can go without blowing a whistle.'

‌



"Done that a few times in the Premier, before VAR obviously. Went 20–25 minutes without blowing a whistle a few times. Let it go, let it go, let it go.

Hugh Jackman reveals talks to buy into Championship club to rival Ryan Reynolds READ MORE :

Ismaila Sarr dream transfer amid Liverpool interest as stance perfectly clear READ MORE :

"I used to do another thing in the Premier League. I used to stand in the centre circle and see how long I could stay in the centre circle before I had to leave. That was just me joking about. The lads used to be on the line saying 'you can't'. I said 'I'll try it'. I just used to run around but don't come out of it. Got about 15 minutes once in one game, without leaving the centre circle."

Such comments have caused some outrage among the football community with calls for the FA to launch an investigation, while two former referees have openly criticised Dean as a result.

‌



Former Premier League referee Graham Scott labelled the claims from Dean about games within matches as ‘nonsense’.

“I worked with Mike [Dean] loads at times, they’re not true stories,” Scott told talkSPORT.

“It’s kind of the audio equivalent of clickbait isn’t it, to try and get people interested and laughing. It’s palpable nonsense.

‌



“Mike Dean [was] of course an outstanding ref, but it makes it so much harder when retired referees either bash their former colleagues for the sake of it.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



“It’s fine to criticise, I do that, but do it with a bit of context and a bit of empathy.”

Scott later added: “I challenge Mike and say, ‘Okay, would you stand in front of the current refs and repeat all of those things?’

“And of course he wouldn’t, because they’re not true.”

‌



Mark Halsey, another former Premier League referee, was in disbelief at the comments made by Dean.

“All my years as a professional referee, I have to say I’ve never heard of these games. Never,” Halsey told BBC Sport.

View 2 Images Mike Dean (Image: Richard Heathcote/Getty Images)

‌

“And I have to say that I have never, ever thought about playing any sort of game, going out to referee.

“Because they’re massive games, you’ve got the fans, you’ve got the players, you’ve got the managers, the delegates, the coaches.

‌



“So I’m astounded, and if Mike has played these games, then he’s done that on his own accord.

“And if he has, then I think we need to know what games he’s done them in? How many games he’s done them in?

“And it brings into question the integrity of every official.”

Sports.title: Hugh Jackman reveals talks to buy into Championship club to rival Ryan Reynolds
Sports.content:
Hugh Jackman reveals talks to buy into Championship club to rival Ryan Reynolds

X-Men star Hugh Jackman has hinted that he could soon be involved with a Championship club and rival Ryan Reynolds' Wrexham team in the race for promotion to the Premier League

View 2 Images Hugh Jackman could follow Ryan Reynolds' by buying into a Championship club (Image: (Photo by Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Offside via Getty Images))

Hugh Jackman could become the latest Hollywood star to buy into a football club after confirming he is in talks to purchase a stake in Norwich City.

‌



The Australian actor, best known for playing Wolverine in the X-Men franchise, is close friends with Ryan Reynolds, who bought Wrexham alongside Rob McElhenney back in 2021. The duo have overseen three successive promotions, taking Wrexham from non-league to the Championship between 2022 and 2025. The Red Dragons ended last season in seventh place, missing out on the Championship play-offs on the final day.

‌



Reynolds and McElhenney's success at Wrexham has been the catalyst for an influx of celebrity investment among EFL clubs - and Jackman has hinted he could become the latest.

‌



The 57-year-old Canaries fan, whose mother was born in Norwich, confirmed talks to talkSPORT when he was asked about getting involved with an English football club, saying: "I'm very, very interested - and talking about it right now.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"Good on Ryan, you do your thing, I'm all about the Canaries."

‌



He added: "I went to Carrow Road a couple of times, and I love the Canaries, and this is the year we're going to get promoted. That's my prediction. My prediction is Norwich and Wrexham are getting promoted this year."

Jackman, who starred alongside Reynolds in the Hollywood blockbuster Deadpool & Wolverine, attended a Wrexham match alongside the Canadian A-Lister back in 2023.

View 2 Images Norwich are expected to challenge for promotion in the Championship this season (Image: Getty)

‌



His bid to become involved with the Norfolk outfit would likely see he and Reynolds go head to head in the race to win promotion to the Premier League with Norwich expected to be among the teams in the mix.

Jackman previously confirmed he had turned down a chance to invest in Norwich more than a decade ago. Speaking back in 2011, he said: "Sometimes I make big mistakes. I got a letter about a year ago saying, being such a huge Norwich City fan would I like to be a celebrity investor? Like a small part-owner.

"I said, 'I think that's a little stretched, I've been to Carrow Road once, my mum took me,' so I decided not to invest. And since then they're on a run, so what do I know?"

Sports.title: Trainer Mickey Bowen announces move to RoseWill Stables purchased by private investor
Sports.content:
Trainer Mickey Bowen announces move to RoseWill Stables purchased by private investor

Bowen started his career at his family’s yard in West Wales last year. Soon he will be on the move to a newly-named facility in Worcestershire

View Image Trainer Mickey Bowen (Image: Shutterstock)

Mickey Bowen has announced he is moving his racehorse training business from Wales to Worcestershire.

‌



The top equine handler, who sits second in the jumps championship after his yard made a bright start to the season, has decided to relocate to Hanley Swan.

‌



Tyre Hill Stables, which used to be the base for David Dennis, was marketed with a price guide of £2.2 million by Windsor Clive International and a sale was agreed with a private investor.

‌



The yard, which has 64 boxes, an equine pool, solarium, two cantering areas and a six-furlong Polytrack gallop across 96 acres, has since been renamed RoseWill Stables.

Bowen said: "We're incredibly excited to be bringing our loyal existing owners with us to RoseWill Stables, while also welcoming new owners to join us on this exciting new chapter.

‌



"This move gives us the opportunity to build something truly special.

"With the quality of horses that we now have, it will be much easier to campaign them from Worcestershire, giving us excellent access to the country's major racecourses while continuing to provide first class facilities at home."

Tom Windsor Clive, spokesman for the equestrian property agents, said: "We had interest from a wide spectrum of the professional horse world, particularly racehorse trainers and eventers. The sellers are delighted to see the yard being brought back into its proper use".

Mickey, whose brothers Sean and James are jockeys, began his career at the family's yard in Haverfordwest, Pembrokeshire.

Like his father Peter, he learned his trade in point-to-points are the pair shared the licence during the 2024-5 jump season when the business made its greatest gains for six years.

Sports.title: 5 worst footballing opinions given new 'walk of shame' award by Alan Shearer
Sports.content:
5 worst footballing opinions given new 'walk of shame' award by Alan Shearer

Alan Shearer has been granted a star on the 'Walk of Shame' outside Wembley Stadium for one of his worst football opinions in a new tongue-in-cheek installation

View 3 Images Alan Shearer hopes his prediction was just 12 months early rather than wrong (Image: Betfair)

Alan Shearer is among the pundits and former players who have been granted stars on Betfair's newly launched 'Walk of Shame' on Wembley Way outside the national stadium.

‌



However, his claim that Newcastle United would beat Sunderland in both of last season's Tyne–Wear derbies - before they lost each game - does not make the top five of worst football opinions of all time. The ranking is based on research conducted with YouGov, which polled 2,008 adult fans across Great Britain.

‌



Alan Hansen and Roy Keane, however, do feature. Two of the takes are about Erling Haaland, with content creators included as well.

‌



Alan Shearer confirms real reason he is scaling back BBC Match of the Day appearances READ MORE :

Alan Shearer leaves Bruno Guimaraes in no doubt after leaving Newcastle for Arsenal READ MORE :

Number five is Hansen's infamous phrase, "You can't win anything with kids". It was uttered on Match of the Day about Manchester United after Sir Alex Ferguson's young side lost 3-1 against Aston Villa on the opening day of the 1995/96 season.

Despite having an average age of 26 years and 137 days - when considering players who made 10 or more appearances - they won the Premier League and FA Cup double. They were the youngest to do so for almost a decade, until Jose Mourinho's first Chelsea team won the title with an average age of 25 years and 312 days.

Coming in at four is 'Rory Talks Football ', an Arsenal supporter who said last year that the Gunners "finishing second was a better achievement than Leicester City winning the league". The Gunners were not 5000/1 with bookmakers to come second when they achieved that 'feat', that is for sure.

‌



3 View 3 Images Alan Shearer avoided his take making the top five, unlike 'Humzy' and 'Rory Talks Football' (Image: Betfair) 3 View 3 Images Alan Shearer joked "What fool said that?" when reading the quote on his star on Betfair's 'Walk of Shame' (Image: Betfair)

Third is where Keane fell for when he said Haaland is "almost like a League Two player". He made the comparison two years ago after a 0-0 draw between Arsenal and Manchester City.

‌



However, it is worth noting that the pundit drew those parallels when discussing his poor general play. In the same breath, he said that "in front of the goal, he's the best in the world ".

The top two are reserved for content creators, with Man United fan 'Humzy' in second for saying last year that "Ruben Amorim's legacy at Man United will be greater than Pep Guardiola's at Man City". Rory Jennings takes top spot for simply saying in 2022 that "Haaland will flop in the Premier League".

‌



Shearer may not have made the top five, but is still holding out hope that his prediction about Sunderland struggling was just early rather than wrong.

The Betfair ambassador said: "What fool said that? Let's hope I was just 12 months early in my prediction.

"It will be a more challenging season for Sunderland this year than it was last year. I do think it will be tougher times for Newcastle as well, and we'll have to be patient, so let's wait and see. We all think we know what's going to happen. But even the best of us can completely miss the mark."
