World.title: Discovery Bank records R370m profit
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Discovery Bank has reported its first profit, posting earnings of R370-million.

This helped the financial services group -- which still includes South Africa’s largest health-insurance administrator, but now also offers insurance and banking -- deliver another year of strong growth.

Discovery Group achieved 17 percent growth in normalised operating profit, reaching R17.7-billion for the year ended June.

Normalised headline earnings per share grew by 20 percent.

Both Discovery’s local and international operations saw solid growth.

Discovery has expanded into Africa, the UK, Europe, Asia, Canada, and the US, and its Vitality unit operates in more than 40 international markets.

The company’s share price closed up almost three percent on the JSE.

World.title: New Zealand approves use of party drug MDMA to treat trauma
World.content:
WELLINGTON - Two psychiatrists in New Zealand won approval to prescribe pharmaceutical-grade MDMA to sufferers of severe post-traumatic stress disorder.

The move by New Zealand's pharmaceutical regulatory body Medsafe makes the country only the second worldwide to approve the use of the party drug for use in treating PTSD, following Australia in 2023.

"PTSD ruins lives and is difficult to treat," said Deputy Prime Minister David Seymour, who last year backed the approval of magic mushrooms to treat people with severe depression.

"MDMA can be very effective at treating it through psychedelic-assisted therapy."

New Zealand is committed to opening up access to "innovative treatments", Seymour said.

PTSD is a mental health condition that develops after a person experiences or is threatened by traumatic events such as death, combat or sexual assault.

Clinical trials are ongoing in the United States after the Federal Drug Administration rejected legalising MDMA's medicinal use in 2024, saying there was not enough evidence it was safe or effective.

Pharmaceutical treatment options for PTSD in the United States have so far been limited to two antidepressants that require three months of dosing to take effect, and response rates to the medications have been uneven.

A study in Israel last year found that MDMA taken by ravers at the Nova music festival when hundreds were killed by Hamas have been helpful in cushioning the impact of the trauma they endured.

Wellington's Ministry of Health said MDMA-assisted treatment would be combined with psychotherapy and stressed that patients would not be supplied drugs to take home.

"Treatment takes place in a controlled clinical setting under the care of an authorised psychiatrist and forms part of a comprehensive treatment plan," the ministry said.

Any patients would have to be aged 18 or older, it added.

World.title: Peet Viljoen back in dock for fraud case
World.content:
PRETORIA - Disbarred lawyer and reality TV personality Peet Viljoen is back before the Specialised Commercial Crimes Court in Pretoria on Friday.

He remains behind bars after being denied bail last month.

Viljoen faces nearly 400 charges, including fraud, corruption, theft, forgery, and uttering.

The charges stem from the alleged sale of municipal properties worth R27 million in 2010, with the long-running case now back in the spotlight.

When bail was denied, the magistrate cited Viljoen as a flight risk and raised concerns that he had intimidated state witnesses.

The state is expected to disclose the contents of the docket when court resumes on Friday, potentially shedding more light on the allegations against the former lawyer and reality TV personality.

World.title: Convicted paedophile Iain Wares to be sentenced in child abuse case
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Convicted paedophile Iain Wares is back at the Wynberg Magistrate’s Court on Friday, where he is expected to be sentenced for child sexual abuse.

The offences were committed during the 1980s.

The 87-year-old was convicted in March 2026 following a case that has drawn renewed attention to allegations spanning decades.

Wares is also wanted in the United Kingdom in connection with more than 90 alleged sexual offences against children.

However, the case has been marked by delays linked to Wares’ health, prompting concern from child rights organisations over the pace of proceedings.

Friday’s sentencing hearing could mark a significant step towards bringing the long-running case to a close.

World.title: Lone juror blocking verdict in US mother's child murder trial: defense
World.content:
PLYMOUTH - The defense for Lindsay Clancy, the US mother accused of murdering her three children, on Thursday accused a single holdout juror of blocking a verdict in the high-profile trial.

Clancy does not deny strangling Cora, five, Dawson, three, and Callan, eight months, but claims she was suffering from postpartum psychosis -- excusing her from criminal responsibility.

Her five-week trial, which was televised and featured more than 80 witnesses, has sparked debate in the United States over maternal mental health.

Kevin Reddington, Clancy's main lawyer, told a Massachusetts court that there is "one juror who refuses to listen to the law that you've given him or her on reasonable doubt."

He requested that the juror be removed from the 12-member panel, but Judge William Sullivan refused and instead sent them back to continue a seventh day of deliberations Friday.

To reach a verdict, all 12 jurors must be in agreement.

If they cannot agree, the judge will declare a mistrial and prosecutors must decide whether to try the case again with a new jury.

On Wednesday, Sullivan issued the jurors a last-resort, so-called "dynamite charge" that encourages them to keep discussing in a bid to break the impasse and avoid a mistrial.

Clancy has pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity, saying she heard a voice ordering her to kill her children. Her lawyers say this was caused by postpartum psychosis.

After the killings at her family home in Duxbury, Massachusetts in January 2023, she jumped from a second-story window in an apparent suicide attempt that left her paralysed from the waist down.

The former nurse faces life in prison without the possibility of parole if found guilty of first-degree murder.

Jurors can also find Clancy guilty of second-degree murder, manslaughter, or not guilty by lack of criminal responsibility -- a verdict that would see Clancy sent to a psychiatric facility.

World.title: Mpumalanga cop arrested in diesel truck hijacking investigation
World.content:
SECUNDA - A police sergeant has been arrested after investigators allegedly uncovered his involvement in a plot to hijack a diesel truck.

The 44-year-old member of the Mpumalanga Flying Squad was arrested during an early-morning operation at the Secunda Police Station.

He is one of five suspects arrested in connection with the alleged hijacking, which took place in May.

Mpumalanga police spokesperson Colonel Mavela Masondo said the involvement of a police officer came to light during the investigation following the arrest of the other four suspects.

“Following the arrest of the four other suspects, the investigation revealed that there was a police officer involved in the planning of the hijacking,” Masondo said.

The sergeant is expected to make his first appearance in court on Monday.

The investigation into the alleged hijacking scheme is continuing, and police said more arrests are expected.

World.title: Three meth labs in four months: Are remote farms becoming drug factories?
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A series of crystal meth laboratories uncovered on remote farms in South Africa is raising questions about the country’s growing role in the production and trafficking of synthetic drugs.

Police uncovered the latest suspected lab during an overnight raid on a farm about 200 kilometres north of Johannesburg, after residents reported suspicious activity and a strong, unpleasant smell.

A 62-year-old man who was renting the property was arrested.

Police say they found equipment and materials believed to have been used to manufacture crystal methamphetamine.

North West police chief Arthur Peter Adams says investigators also found expensive equipment, including recently purchased washing machines.

“That is an indication that whoever is funding this is a person with very deep pockets,” Adams said.

World.title: Phala Phala report review: MK Party, UAT to present arguments
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - The legal battle over the Phala Phala farm theft independent panel report continues at the Western Cape High Court on Friday, with the MK Party and United Africans Transformation (UAT) set to present their arguments.

The proceedings follow Thursday’s focus on the stashed US dollars and the Namibian connection at the centre of the controversy.

Lawyers debated the origins of the cash and questioned trips to Namibia involving former special envoy Bejani Chauke and Presidential Protection Services head, Major-General Wally Rhoode.

President Cyril Ramaphosa is asking the Western Cape High Court to set aside the report of the independent panel, which concluded that he may have violated the Constitution and his oath of office in his handling of the theft at his Phala Phala farm.

As arguments continue on Friday, the court battle could further intensify scrutiny of the president’s conduct and the unanswered questions surrounding the cash, the theft, and the events that followed.

World.title: From a 'pumbafu' driver to abductions master: How Zachary Kariuki rose from Kibaki's driver to head dreaded squad
World.content:
Zachary Kiago Kariuki retired in 2025 and was appointed two years ago to be in charge of a unit in the DCI. [Courtesy, Standard]

President Mwai Kibaki once called his driver "bure...pumbafu sana". The crowd in attendance went wild with laughter and when the event was broadcast, so did the nation. The moniker pumbafu became an everyday insult, albeit jokingly. What Kenyans did not know was that the object of the insult was one Zachary Kariuki. Kariuki was President Kibaki's driver and had parked the armoured vehicle on grass. Rain was about to fall and because of the weight of the vehicle, Kariuki thought it would be difficult to move it once the ground was soggy. For his wisdom, he became the laughing stock.

World.title: Ruto assures Kajiado residents of full control of Amboseli National Park
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto inspects the Rombo Clusters Irrigation Development Project in Kajiado County on September 3, 2026. [Peterson Githaiga, Standard]

President William Ruto has assured Kajiado residents that they will soon have full control of the management of Amboseli National Park, following his decision to return the park to the county in November 2025.

However, he said the transfer has been temporarily halted by the court.

The President hit out at those he accused of frustrating the move, saying they will be in for a rude shock.

“They took us to court over the Social Health Authority and the Affordable Housing Programme, but these programmes are progressing well. Similarly, I want to assure the people of Kajiado that, before the end of this year, Amboseli will be fully in the hands of Kajiado County,” he said.

Speaking in Kajiado County on Thursday during his development tour, President Ruto reiterated that he will not relent in his pursuit of equity and inclusive development across Kenya, saying that longstanding inequalities have unduly benefited certain regions at the expense of others.

He revealed that the securitisation of the Road Maintenance Levy Fund and the Sports Fund has enabled the Government to clear pending bills in the roads sector and construct 6,000km of new roads, and accelerate the construction of 32 new stadia across the country.

"The Road Maintenance Levy Fund was misused to only build roads in some parts of the country. Those opposing securitisation are unhappy that we are advancing equity," he said.

The President began his tour at Oloirien in Kajiado South Constituency by inspecting progress of the 67km Illasit-Rombo-Chala-Njukini-Taveta road, which is 48 per cent completed.

The Sh9.4 billion project will cut travel time between Kajiado and Taita-Taveta counties from two hours to just 40 minutes, thus easing the movement of goods and people.

The Head of State announced that eight new roads of 220km are being built across Kajiado County at a cost of Sh13 billion to open up the region and improve transport.

The President commissioned Sh221 million Rombo Clusters Irrigation Development Project, which is expected to enhance livelihoods and boost irrigation in the area.

He also inspected progress of the Sh2.2 billion Loitoktok Affordable Housing Project, and laid the foundation stone for the Sh220 million Loitoktok Kenya Medical Training College student hostels with a 580-bed capacity.

At Kimana, in Kajiado South Constituency, President Ruto commissioned the Sh2.7 billion Sultan Hamud-Loitoktok 132kV Transmission Line and Loitoktok Sub-Station, which will serve the residents of Kajiado South and parts of Makueni County.

He inspected construction of the Kimana modern market, which is aimed at giving traders dignified working environment.

At Namanga, Kajiado Central Constituency, the President commissioned the Namanga Sub-Station, a project of the Kenya Electricity Transmission Company (KETRACO), which is part of the 132KV Machakos- Konza-Isinya-Namanga Transmission Project.

Namanga Modern Market, which is under construction at a cost of Sh50 million, will benefit 120 traders at the border town.

In Kajiado town, the President toured the construction of the Kajiado Affordable Housing Project, a Sh473 million investment that will deliver 196 housing units, as well as the 100-unit police housing project at a cost of Sh137 million.

He also inspected the progress of the 580-bed student hostels at Maasai National Polytechnic, which is being built at a cost of KSh216 million.

Ruto ordered the closer of Tata Chemicals, saying the government will identify a new and responsible investor to take over soda ash mining operations at Lake Magadi.

The President said Tata Chemicals had failed to adequately modernise the plant, create sufficient employment opportunities for residents, and deliver meaningful economic benefits to the people of Kenya.

“It is unfair for one company to dominate the ownership and operations of Magadi Soda for years, yet it has done little to improve the factory or create employment opportunities for our youth,” he said at Rombo in Kajiado South Constituency.

He added: “Because they have been unable to do anything meaningful with the plant for more than 100 years, I have directed them to pack up and go.”

The Ministry of Mining suspended the company’s mining operations in July 2026 over concerns relating to regulatory compliance, value addition and licensing.

The ministry also ordered the closure of the company’s depot in Kajiado Town for contravening environmental regulations.

In addition, the company has been unable to reach an agreement with the Kajiado County Government over a land rates dispute following the expiry of its operating licence in 2023.

The plant produces soda ash, or sodium carbonate, a key industrial mineral used in the manufacture of glass, soap and laundry detergents, among other products.

Despite being Africa’s largest soda ash producer, President Ruto noted that the operation had not delivered commensurate benefits to Kenyans over its more than 100-year history, particularly because much of the soda ash produced is exported for processing and consumption in overseas markets.

The Government, the President said, would therefore prioritise an investor capable of modernising the facility, expanding local value addition, creating jobs for young people, and ensuring that Kenya derives greater economic value from its natural resources.

World.title: IG Kanja orders probe into abduction of Standard Group Associate Editor
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Standard Group PLC Associate Editor Alex Kiprotich. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja has ordered immediate and transparent investigations into the alleged abduction of Standard Group Associate Editor Alex Kiprotich in Gilgil.

The National Police Service (NPS) said it had taken note of reports that Kiprotich was allegedly kidnapped on Tuesday and had moved swiftly to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

NPS spokesperson Muchiri Nyaga said the police service treats kidnapping and abduction with the utmost seriousness, describing the offences as a threat to the lives, liberty and security of Kenyans.

“The Inspector General of Police has accordingly ordered immediate investigations to determine what transpired, including the identity of the heavily armed individuals reportedly seen ordering occupants out of their vehicle,” Nyaga said in a statement.

The NPS said its Anti-Abduction Unit, established to investigate abductions and disappearances, had taken up the matter and would work to ensure that those responsible are brought to justice.

“We unequivocally condemn any act of kidnapping, abduction, or intimidation intended to interfere with press freedom or any other constitutional right,” Nyaga said.

The police service assured the public that the investigation into the Gilgil incident would be conducted transparently, stressing that no one was above the law.

The development comes amid growing condemnation of Kiprotich’s alleged abduction, with the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) also calling for an immediate investigation.

CPJ Africa Director Angela Quintal described the incident as a “shameful indictment” of the Kenya Kwanza administration, raising concerns over the safety of journalists and press freedom in the country.

“The attempt to forcibly disappear Alex Kiprotich, three days after President William Ruto railed against The Standard Group, reflects the growing dangers that journalists face in Kenya, despite the president’s earlier promise to allow the press to work freely,” Quintal said.

The New York-based press freedom organisation further expressed concern over what it described as an escalation in cases of abductions and enforced disappearances in Kenya.

World.title: Ruto hands Sh2.6bn to Mau Forest evictees
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto also announced the lifting pf the caveat that had been placed on land bordering the Mau Forest. [PCS]

President William Ruto has announced the payment of Sh2.6 billion to 13,000 families evicted from the Mau Forest in Narok six years ago, marking what he described as the closure of a long chapter.

Each beneficiary received Sh200,000 through M-Pesa to help them resettle and rebuild their lives away from the water tower.

Speaking at Sogoo in Narok South Constituency on Wednesday, during the final day of his two-day tour of Narok County, Ruto said the Government had taken steps to address the longstanding Mau Forest resettlement problem.

He noted that in 2023, the Government gave Sh300,000 each to 2,000 families living in tents in the Mau Forest to enable them to leave the water tower and purchase land elsewhere.

“We are today officially closing the long and painful chapter of people who were removed from the Mau Forest, which the County Government of Narok will now manage,” Ruto said.

The President criticised politicians who, he said, had continued to politicise the Mau Forest issue without providing lasting solutions.

“Many politicians have talked of the Mau question, but I talked of the Mau answer. This is why we are here today closing this chapter,” he said.

Ruto also announced that the Government had purchased 5,800 acres of land to settle families who have been living as squatters on property previously owned by the family of former Provincial Commissioner Isaiah Cheluget.

“We are processing title deeds of the people living on the land after buying the Cheluget farm,” he said.

Construction of Johanna Ng'eno University

The President also announced the allocation of Sh1.2 billion for the construction of Johanna Ng’eno University in Emurua Dikirr Constituency.

Speaking during the laying of the foundation stone, Ruto said the institution would fulfil a pledge to residents while expanding access to higher education for students from across the country.

“You told me, as residents of Emurua Dikirr, that you want a university. Today, I have brought KSh1.2 billion to construct the university that will be named after our brother Johana Ng'eno,” he said.

He said the university would create employment opportunities and attract new investments to the region.

At the same time, Ruto maintained that his administration had fulfilled at least 80 per cent of the pledges contained in its 2022 campaign manifesto.

“Kenyans will elect leaders based on their development record. Sloganeering will not make Kenyans vote for them. They have a long way to go,” he said.

The President further launched the construction of the 18-kilometre Mogondo-Cheramgoi-Mogor-Soit road in Emurua Dikirr, saying the project would improve connectivity and unlock economic opportunities in the region.

“This new road will strengthen connectivity and unlock greater economic opportunities in the region,” Ruto said.

World.title: Gachagua to Duale: You don't own pastoralists
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua and delegates from Isiolo and Marsabit at Wamunyoro, Nyeri County on August 25, 2026. [Ali Abdi, Standard]

Democracy for Citizen Party (DCP) Leader Rigathi Gachagua has accused Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale of allegedly doing nothing for pastoralist communities in the country.

Mr Gachagua said Duale, while being the only CS from northern Kenya and claiming to be the spokesperson of the group, had instead been a liability to pastoralists.

“You, the Borana who are here, along with the Turkana and Somali, are all complaining like other Kenyans. You suffer from runaway insecurity and widespread underdevelopment. We must join hands to vote out this rogue government (in next year's general election),” the former Deputy President told a delegation of grassroots leaders and residents from Isiolo and Marsabit who paid him a courtesy call at his Wamunyoro rural home in Nyeri.

“Duale thinks that the pastoralists are his property, his children or servants. What has he done for the people of Isiolo and Marsabit? (He has) only rhetoric, shouting pastoralists everywhere, every day,” he said.

Gachagua questioned how Duale would be able to marshal ‘millions’ of votes for President Ruto in the 2027 General Elections while he (Duale) could only raise 7,000 votes for the UDA presidential candidate in the 2022 polls in his Garissa Township Constituency backyard.

Despite his little contribution to the Kenya Kwanza administration's victory, Gachagua said Duale was appointed as the only CS from northern Kenya but had ended up doing nothing for the region and pastoralist communities.

“He only gave him (Ruto) 7,000 votes in Garissa Township. It's Central Kenya that propelled this government,” Gachagua told the gathering.

“Duale was appointed CS and he has nothing to show apart from empty words, going round shouting (the name of) pastoralists, and you (the pastoralists) are suffering. If you love them, then why are their livestock stolen every day?” He asked the CS.

“These pastoralists are killed every day and their cows and goats stolen. What have you done for them and you are in the government?” Gachagua posed.

The Opposition leader claimed that the government was ill-prepared for the heavily forecasted El Niño rainfall, pointing out that those living in flood-prone areas like the Tana Delta and Garissa are exposed to danger.

“Now, going into El Niño, what plan has been put in place to save people from death as a result of floods and how livestock will survive?” he asked the State.

During the event, Gachagua revealed that Yusuf Huka Jillo from Isiolo would represent Upper Eastern at the DCP secretariat and serve as a member of the National Executive Committee (NEC) in an acting capacity.

Gachagua said the mountain was now complete, with Isiolo and Marsabit forming Mt Kenya North.

The locals alleged that the Health CS was interfering in Isiolo County politics, with elder Hussein Jama claiming that Duale and the Office of the DCI were shielding a section of leaders accused of corruption and criminal activities.

Speakers claimed that there was massive corruption at the local lands registry office, while Mr Jillo faulted the State for the slow pace of registration of community land in Isiolo.

Jama said Isiolo International Airport, which was constructed during the administration of President Kibaki to help in the export of miraa and horticultural goods from the Mt Kenya region and livestock products, mainly meat and hides, lies idle because the expansion of the runway from 1.5 metres to 3 metres had not been done.

In response, Gachagua said the airport was meant to create employment and wealth, but the Kenya Kwanza administration had instead left it in ruin deliberately, claiming the move was aimed at sabotaging the economy of Mt Kenya and pastoralists’ economies.

“What was the good about destroying the Imenti forest to construct an airstrip for an individual while there is an international airport meant partly to serve the entire region just a few kilometres from Meru town?” Asked the DCP leader.

World.title: Relief for schools as government releases Sh18.5b capitation
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Education CS Julius Ogamba. [File, Standard]

The government has released Sh18.5 billion in capitation to support operations in public basic education institutions during the third term of 2026, as schools reopened across the country on Monday.

Education Cabinet Secretary Julius Ogamba said the funds have already been released and will support learners in pre-primary, primary, junior and senior schools.

The allocation is intended to facilitate smooth school operations and ensure learning activities continue without disruption.

The Sh18.5 billion has been distributed across three major capitation programmes, with Free Day Secondary Education (FDSE) allocated Sh10.963 billion, accounting for the biggest portion of the Term Three capitation.

The money will support operations in public day and secondary schools and comes as institutions prepare learners for a busy academic term.

Free Day Junior School Education has received Sh6.1 billion, to support learners in the second tier of basic education and help institutions meet operational requirements as the Competency-Based Education system continues to expand.

Meanwhile, Free Primary Education has been allocated Sh1.4 billion to support learning in public primary schools.

The funds come as a relief to school heads who had raised concerns on the insufficient funds disbursed to schools this year.

However, Ogamba said the disbursement demonstrates the Government's commitment to ensuring that learners have access to free and compulsory basic education as provided for under Article 53(1)(b) of the Constitution.

“The Government affirms its commitment to fulfil its duty to learners and educational institutions,” said the CS.

Ogamba also warned school heads and principals against misuse of the funds, directing them to ensure the money is spent prudently and for the benefit of learners.

School administrators have further been cautioned against imposing unauthorised levies on parents and learners.

Ogamba said the Ministry would take firm action against institutions found to have misappropriated public resources or imposed illegal charges.

“We will deal firmly with any verified cases of misappropriation of resources and the imposition of unauthorised levies,” he said.

The warning comes as schools reopen for the third term, a period that is expected to be particularly demanding for institutions and learners because of the academic activities and assessments scheduled for the school calendar.

The Ministry has maintained that capitation is meant to ease the financial burden on families and enable schools to provide essential services without passing prohibited costs to parents.

Ogamba reiterated that school administrators must remain accountable for the public funds entrusted to them, warning that verified cases of misuse will attract action from the Ministry.

The Government has also reaffirmed that every child is entitled to free and compulsory basic education, placing the responsibility on education officials and school managers to ensure capitation achieves its intended purpose.

World.title: Ndindi Nyoro begins nationwide political mobilisation ahead of 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro after attending service at Gathuki-ini ACK Church on August 23, 2026. [Boniface Gikandi, Standard]

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro has said he will take his campaign for national transformation across Kenya as he positions himself for the 2027 presidential race.

Ndindi said he was interested in leadership committed to addressing concerns in education, health, youth and unemployment, among other needs.

Nyoro, who is the People’s Party of Kenya leader, spoke at St Michael Gathuki-ini ACK Church in Kiharu on Sunday, where he called for respect and political maturity.

Addressing residents in Kiria-ini (Mathioya) and Gakira (Kangema), he urged politicians to engage in a responsible manner.

“I trust in God that after next year Kenya will be able to have leadership that will be responsible for improving citizens' standards of living,” he said.

He regretted that hundreds of university graduates in the area were yet to secure employment.

“I plead with Kenyans to support my course that is geared to transform the nation and ensure equality and transparency,” said the PPK leader.

Nyoro said that after engaging Murang'a residents, he will take his transformation campaigns to all parts of the country.

Speaking at Kiria-ini market, he said he would engage the people to seek their blessings.

“All along had been feeling the urge to lead the country, thus the need to come out in the open and fight for position,” he said.

On Monday, the MP announced his exit from the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA), declaring that he will join the opposition ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Nyoro, an economist serving his second term as Kiharu MP, said he will work with opposition leaders to push for what he termed real change in Kenya.

The legislator said all opposition presidential aspirants are welcome at rallies organised by the PPK.

His move marks a significant political shift as parties and leaders begin positioning themselves ahead of the 2027 polls.

World.title: City Hall in rush to expand drainage system ahead of El Nino
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja during an inspection tour of the ongoing drainage system expansion. [GPS]

Nairobi County has embarked on drainage expansion works aimed at mitigating floodwaters ahead of El Nino rains.

Governor Johnson Sakaja, while calling on city residents to remain alert and proactive, said City Hall has intensified preparations and accelerated identification of hotspots.

The governor on Friday said his administration is taking early and coordinated action to minimise the impact of heavy rains, urging residents to stay calm, pay attention to official information and follow guidance from the multi-agency team established to coordinate the city’s preparedness and emergency response.

“We are working proactively to address the challenges of flooding before El Nino hits the ground. We urge our people not to panic but to be alert and get information from our multi-agency team,” said Sakaja.

The Governor spoke during an inspection tour of several flood-prone areas in Nairobi, including the Mombasa Road-Bunyala Junction corridor and Globe Roundabout, which experienced significant flooding during previous heavy rains.

Sakaja said drainage works are already underway in the affected areas, with teams working to open up and deepen drainage channels, clear obstructions, and improve storm-water flow to prevent a repeat of the flooding witnessed previously.

His remarks come as weatherman warned of increased rainfall in the coming months, with Nairobi among the urban areas requiring heightened preparedness because of its exposure to flooding and the impact of heavy rainfall on roads, settlements and other critical infrastructure.

Sakaja said the county has so far brought together the disaster management teams, Kenya Red Cross, Kenya Urban Roads Authority (KURA) and Kenya National Highways Authority (KeNHA) under a coordinated programme worth Sh2.4 billion to strengthen Nairobi’s flood resilience.

Of the amount, Sh2 billion has been set aside for drainage and flood-mitigation works targeting 19 roads in flood-prone areas.

The projects are at an advanced stage, with tenders awarded and contractors expected to commence implementation after completion of the necessary processes.

Sakaja reiterated that the programme will complement ongoing county interventions under the Nairobi Regeneration Programme, which includes the rehabilitation and upgrading of critical infrastructure across the city.

“The Sh2 billion will support a comprehensive drainage overhaul that complements the ongoing Nairobi Regeneration Programme. Our goal is to permanently address the flooding challenges that have affected the city for many years,” Sakaja said.

He said the focus is not only on responding to floods after they occur, but on addressing the infrastructure weaknesses that have historically made Nairobi vulnerable to flooding.

To strengthen preparedness, the county has established five specialised sub-committees under the multi-agency framework.

The committees include Infrastructure and Drainage; Emergency Response and Evacuation; Shelter and Relief; Security and Traffic and Communication.

While the Infrastructure and Drainage committee will coordinate the clearing and improvement of drainage systems, rivers and other critical infrastructure, the Emergency Response and Evacuation committee will oversee rapid response, rescue and evacuation operations whenever emergencies occur.

The Shelter and Relief committee will prepare safe shelters and coordinate the provision of food, water, medical assistance and other essential support to affected residents.

The Security and Traffic committee will coordinate security, traffic management and emergency access, while the Communication committee will strengthen early-warning systems, public alerts and timely dissemination of information.

Sakaja said the county is also mobilising personnel, equipment and other resources to clear blocked drains, remove silt and waste and strengthen emergency response systems in areas identified as vulnerable.

He urged residents and their associations, businesses and other stakeholders to play an active role in flood preparedness by keeping drainage areas clear and paying attention to official warnings.

The county chief said residents in high-risk areas will be provided with timely information on emerging weather conditions and the actions they should take when heavy rains occur.

“We don’t want people to panic. We want people to be proactive, to listen to information and to work with us. The multi-agency team is in place, and we are preparing before the rains intensify,” Sakaja said.

According to him, the multi-agency approach will also help eliminate jurisdictional gaps by bringing together national and county agencies to operate as one coordinated team.

He said the combination of drainage upgrades, emergency preparedness, early-warning systems and coordinated response would strengthen Nairobi’s resilience and reduce disruption caused by heavy rains.

The multi-agency team is expected to meet next week to review progress, coordinate ongoing works and further push the city’s El Niño preparedness agenda.

World.title: Nile River is matter of national security, Egypt retains right to defend its waters: Sisi
World.content:
Egypt views the Nile River as a non-negotiable component of its national security, President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi reiterated during high-level discussions in Cairo with Italian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Antonio Tajani.

According to the presidential spokesperson, Sisi underlined Cairo’s legitimate right to safeguard its water, food, and developmental security.

He firmly rejected any unilateral measures along the Nile basin, calling for strict compliance with international law—specifically the core doctrine prohibiting harm to downstream nations.

Beyond the Nile issue, the meeting covered shifting dynamics across the Horn of Africa.

Both officials agreed to step up bilateral coordination to bolster regional stability, emphasizing full respect for the sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of all states in the region.

Turning to maritime security, Sisi stressed that preserving freedom of navigation through international waterways remains vital, highlighting the Red Sea’s strategic role in Egyptian national defense.

The Egyptian President affirmed that securing the Red Sea falls strictly under the jurisdiction of its coastal states, warning against actions that threaten its stability or risk militarizing and internationalizing the key waterway.

World.title: Upgraded Su-57 stealth fighter debuts at Egypt International Airshow with new weaponry
World.content:
Russia’s defense sector is preparing a major technology showcase for the Egypt International Airshow 2026, where state giant Rostec will premiere its export-grade Su-57E fifth-generation stealth fighter equipped with a previously unseen armaments package, TASS reported.

The upcoming event, scheduled for September 8–10 in El Alamein, will serve as the launchpad for the updated Su-57E variant.

Beyond static displays of its newly integrated weapons systems—which have yet to be publicly exhibited inside or outside Russia—the aircraft is slated to perform live aerial demonstrations during the expo.

In tandem with the fighter jet’s debut, Rostec subsidiary High Precision Systems will stage the first foreign demonstration of the “Bison” anti-drone system.

Engineered to intercept and neutralize low-altitude aerial threats and unmanned vehicles, the system will be featured as a core component of Moscow’s defensive systems export portfolio.

World.title: Egypt and China strengthen bilateral security and diplomatic ties
World.content:
Egypt and China issued a comprehensive joint statement reaffirming their shared commitment to stability in the Middle East, calling for a permanent ceasefire in the Gaza Strip, and urging the unhindered flow of humanitarian aid into the besieged enclave.

In the joint declaration, both nations emphasized the critical need to solidify a lasting ceasefire in Gaza while demanding the immediate removal of restrictions hindering aid delivery.

Cairo and Beijing also advocated for the swift return of the Palestinian Authority to govern the Gaza Strip as a vital step toward restoring administrative unity and political stability.

Expressing severe concern over escalating regional tensions, both governments condemned the dangerous military escalation by Israeli forces across the West Bank and East Jerusalem.

They highlighted deep alarm over the rising pace of settler violence, systemic land confiscation, and expanding settlement construction, warning that such actions actively undermine peace prospects.

Egypt and China underscored the paramount importance of safeguarding Palestine’s territorial integrity.

Extending their diplomatic posture to North Africa, both powers called for strict respect for Sudan’s sovereignty, territorial unity, and national institutions, firmly rejecting any external interference in internal Sudanese affairs.

World.title: Will September see any heatwaves?
World.content:
Following the intense heatwaves of August, attention has shifted to the weather outlook for September, with many wondering whether further extreme heat is on the horizon.

According to the Egyptian Meteorological Authority (EMA), weather conditions remain stable across the country.

Daytime temperatures in Cairo are averaging around 35C, though active winds are bringing cooler evening breezes and offering noticeable relief at night.

Meteorologists do not anticipate a return to August’s extreme temperatures. However, high humidity levels could make temperatures feel roughly two degrees warmer than actual recordings.

Dense morning fog remains the primary weather factor to watch throughout September.

Fog formation is expected along agricultural routes, highways, and areas near bodies of water, which may significantly reduce horizontal visibility.

The EMA has urged drivers to exercise caution on the roads.

World.title: Saudi Arabia’s security remains a red line for Egypt: Sisi
World.content:
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi received a phone call today from Saudi Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz al-Saud, according to an official statement by the Spokesperson for the Egyptian Presidency, Mohamed al-Shennawy.

Sisi extended his heartfelt congratulations to the Saudi Crown Prince ahead of the upcoming Saudi National Day.

Egypt’s President wished Saudi Arabia continued stability, prosperity, and development under the leadership of King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.

Expressing his gratitude for the fraternal gesture, the Crown Prince reaffirmed the deeply rooted, historic ties uniting the two nations.

According to al-Shennawy, the discussion covered the full scope of bilateral relations.

President Sisi emphasized the importance of advancing cooperation across various fields to fulfill mutual interests, drive sustainable development, and support regional security.

The Egyptian President also underlined the shared destiny of Egypt and Saudi Arabia, reiterating that the security of Saudi Arabia and the wider Arab region remains an integral pillar of Egyptian national security.

He stressed that joint action is critical to overcoming the current regional challenges.

Reciprocating the sentiment, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman praised the growing trajectory of Saudi-Egyptian relations and the close coordination aimed at fostering peace and stability across the Middle East. He highlighted the need to intensify high-level political consultation and reciprocal visits across multiple domains.

The call also addressed pressing regional and international issues. Both leaders stressed the urgent need to de-escalate ongoing regional tensions to safeguard peace and mitigate risks to global energy security, supply chains, and international trade routes.

World.title: Egyptian court halts trial of manual laborer who impersonated judge in housing scam
World.content:
The Ain Shams Misdemeanor Court has ordered a temporary stay in the trial of a man accused of impersonating a judge, committing real estate fraud, and filming promotional social media videos inside a courthouse while wearing judicial sashes.

The proceedings remain suspended while a higher court evaluates a motion filed by the defense to recuse the judicial panel.

The main defendant, alongside co-conspirators and court staff, will remain in custody throughout the stay.

During the hearing, the primary suspect remained silent when confronted with the official referral order and charges.

The defense counsel argued that the defendant was mentally unsound, pointing to bizarre behavioral patterns—including carrying judicial sashes into public cafes and hiring luxury cars with private guards despite working as a manual bricklayer.

The defense has requested an official psychiatric evaluation to properly determine his mental state.

Prosecution investigations began after online social media reports detailed a housing allocation scam. Authorities subsequently arrested the suspect in possession of an unlicensed firearm, ammunition, counterfeit judicial badges, and judicial sashes.

Analysis of seized phones confirmed recorded footage filmed inside court facilities with complicit personnel.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Nvidia doubles its sales, but investors have their eye on the future
World.content:
New York — Nvidia’s earnings beat expectations and its revenue doubled from a year ago, but it was the potential for future growth that excited investors.

The chipmaker has seen soaring revenue sitting at the head of the AI boom. The company earned $96.2 billion in the most recent quarter, a 106 percent rise from a year ago, according to its earnings report on Wednesday. Revenue from sales to data centers, an overwhelming chunk of its business, was $89 billion, an increase of 117 percent from a year ago.

Despite those blockbuster numbers, shares didn’t take an upward turn until the company’s earnings call on Wednesday evening. CFO Colette Kress told investors that the company expected its fiscal 2028 income to grow by 70 percent. Analysts had expected 45 percent.

Nvidia (NVDA) shares rose more than 4 percent after-hours, reversing course after initially dipping following the earnings release.

Nvidia expects big growth because it is confident in the AI ecosystem’s growth – and its crucial role in it. It’s viewed as a bellwether for the state of the AI market because so much of the industry’s technology runs on its chips.

“Everybody wants to be part of the AI revolution. Everybody will have to be part of this computing shift, and everybody has to build infrastructure,” CEO Jensen Huang said on the earnings call.

The chipmaker is also increasing investments in other tech companies to help fund their AI infrastructure build-outs, spurring criticism of a circular financing strategy. The circular nature of many financing deals has raised concerns that demand for AI may be artificially inflated.

Nvidia and Amazon on Wednesday also announced a new deal that will expand the use of Nvidia’s semiconductor chips across Amazon’s data centers. Amazon Web Service is set to use an additional 2 million of Nvidia’s graphics processing units (GPUs) across its infrastructure. The deal expands on a previous announcement in March that AWS would use 1 million of Nvidia’s GPUs.

Nvidia shares are up about 12 percent this year, roughly in line with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite. After years of enormous gains, Nvidia shares have seen more modest gains this year. Recent quarters have seen Nvidia post better-than-expected results only for its stock to dip following the report.

If Nvidia’s earnings are strong, the thinking goes, other leading tech firms will see sufficient future returns from AI to keep investing in its products — and investors can expect to keep seeing returns from the market.

But building AI infrastructure is incredibly expensive. The so-called hyperscalers that are building out data centers, like Meta, Microsoft and Google, have started to face tough questions from investors about whether those billions in investments will pay off — or if they should pull back their spending.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in Taipei on June 1, 2026. I-Hwa Cheng/AFP/Getty Images

Some market watchers worry that exuberance over AI has bid up tech stocks too high — and that it’s a bubble waiting to burst.

Earlier this month, Nvidia announced a partnership with a group of Wall Street firms to allow its customers to borrow money to buy its products for their AI infrastructure.

Some analysts have questioned whether this circular financing strategy could be risky for Nvidia if those customers don’t see meaningful returns from that infrastructure.

“All of the AI services at some point are going to want to go around the world, and those data centers won’t necessarily be just built by them,” Huang said on Wednesday. “I think they’re going to run on Nvidia.”

World.title: Spain’s PM says he received no advance warnings of Ceuta influx as he defends handling of crisis
World.content:
Spain’s Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has denied accusations that the government ignored warnings about an impending mass border crossing from Morocco to the enclave of Ceuta.

In an address to parliament on Thursday, Sánchez said that there had been no “alerts or special notices” prior to July 30-31, when an estimated 60,000 people entered Ceuta.

“We have examined all of the messages, statements and verbal reports from the state security apparatus,” he said.

“I can assure you that none of them went any further than a description of the data or routine reporting, and that absolutely none of them predicted the probability or the scale of what ended up occurring.”

Sánchez defended his government’s handling of the crisis, and promised to publish a dossier of official reports showing all of the information that was available to the government.

“The government has nothing to hide on this matter,” he said.

Although most of the migrants have since crossed back over the border to Morocco, the incident has become a significant political issue for Sánchez and his government both at home and abroad.

Relations with Morocco have been strained following reports that its government had facilitated the mass border crossing, but Sánchez tamped down the speculation.

“Lots of people think that the Moroccan authorities provoked this crisis,” he said.

“Up to this point, no one has provided any definitive proof to the government that would allow us to conclude that this mass border crossing… was planned or executed by the Moroccan authorities,” he said, adding that investigations were ongoing as to whether they had in fact played any role in the incident.

Sánchez added that the two countries would continue to cooperate on border issues, but “it’s clear that after what happened this cooperation has to be different.”

The incident has also caused diplomatic issues within the European Union (EU), with anti-immigration leaders such as Italy’s Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni calling for Spain’s membership of the Schengen visa-free travel area to be suspended.

The spat became so hostile that Jose Manuel Albares, Spain’s foreign minister, summoned the Italian ambassador on July 31 to discuss comments made by his Italian counterpart Antonio Tajani, who claimed, without evidence, that Madrid’s immigration policy “encourages human trafficking.”

On Thursday, Sánchez said that he would ask for support from EU institutions such as Frontex, the bloc’s border and coastguard agency, in securing borders at both Ceuta and Melilla, Spain’s other enclave on the North African coast. Both are claimed by Morocco.

“We are going to ask that a permanent Frontex presence be established,” he said, as well as requesting a special Europol mission to monitor irregular migration to Ceuta.

The Spanish government will also ask the EU to recognize Ceuta and Melilla as outermost regions of the bloc, a special designation that allows territories that are separate from mainland Europe to join the EU customs union, said Sánchez.

His progressive government is also facing domestic political pressure, with tens of thousands of people taking to the streets of Ceuta and other cities around Spain on Wednesday to protest its handling of the crisis.

An estimated 10,000 migrants remain in Ceuta, which has a permanent population of around 80,000 people, causing social tensions in the enclave and providing a talking point for Spain’s insurgent far-right.

However Sánchez also acknowledged that it is impossible to completely prevent border crossings.

“We aren’t going to guarantee that these borders are 100 percent secure, because behind them lie inequality and a search for opportunity, and no matter how high that border (wall) is, this is always going to be the case,” he said.

This is a developing story and will be updated.

World.title: Liberia: No Ruling as Jewel Howard Taylor’s Lawyers Wait for Judge
World.content:
Monrovia — There was still no ruling Thursday on a motion for compassionate leave filed on behalf of former Vice President Jewel Howard Taylor, as the presiding judge of Criminal Court “C” did not appear in court to hear or deliver a decision on the matter.

The ruling had been scheduled for Thursday, September 3, at Criminal Court “C” at the Temple of Justice in Monrovia.

Taylor’s defense lawyers arrived at the courthouse and remained in the courtroom from approximately 3:00 p.m. until 6:00 p.m., awaiting the judge.

Among the attorneys present were Cllr. Cabina Ja’neh, Cllr. Finley Kangar and Cllr. Lavala Superwood.

Prosecutors were also seen at the court earlier in the day but reportedly left after a few minutes, while Taylor’s defense team remained behind in anticipation of the judge’s appearance.

The lawyers were later seen leaving the courthouse, visibly frustrated, after the judge had not appeared and no ruling had been announced.

The delay leaves unresolved Taylor’s request for compassionate leave, which her lawyers have filed amid concerns about her health and the need for medical treatment.

Taylor remains in detention while facing serious criminal allegations brought against her by the Liberian Government.

Her defense team has maintained that her health situation warrants consideration of compassionate leave and access to appropriate medical care.

The court’s failure to issue a ruling Thursday means Taylor’s immediate legal and medical status remains unchanged, pending further action by the court.
