World.title: Kuressaare residents told to boil water after E. coli, coliform found
World.content:
Coliform bacteria were found across the water network in Kuressaare, Saaremaa's capital, while E. coli was found in two samples. Residents are advised to boil drinking water.

The contamination appears to stem from raw water at the intake rather than within the network, though officials are awaiting repeat samples to confirm the source.

The findings are preliminary, and an official analysis report is not yet available. The municipality has begun preventive chlorination and flushing of the mains.

Saaremaa Municipality recommends boiling water before drinking to ensure it is completely safe. Repeat samples are to be taken immediately.

"The widespread contamination of the water network with coliform bacteria points more to contamination of the raw water coming from the water intake than to contamination occurring within the water network, but it is difficult to assess the causes of the contamination before the results of the repeat samples are available. Kuressaare Veevärk has also informed the Health Board of the situation and coordinated further steps," the municipality said on its website.

Coliform bacteria are common environmental bacteria found, for example, in the external environment, including nutrient‑rich water, wastewater, soil and decomposing plant material. Their presence in water does not generally cause illness in humans, but as an indicator they can provide valuable information about the drinking water distribution network. "The presence of small numbers of coliform bacteria in drinking water primarily indicates a need to flush the pipelines. One way to ensure water purity is to add chlorine to drinking water. Small numbers of coliform bacteria are unlikely to pose a health risk. However, because vulnerable groups require greater protection under the precautionary principle, stricter‑than‑usual measures are applied when they are detected," the municipality's website went on.

E. coli is a species of bacteria that forms part of the natural microbiota of humans and animals. It can enter natural waters and wells, particularly during heavy rainfall or snowmelt, through organic matter washed off the ground. The presence of E. coli in water is primarily a signal that drinking water needs to be checked further and, if necessary, water treatment adjusted. Although most strains of E. coli are completely harmless, certain rare strains can pose a risk of illness. For this reason, every detection is treated with full attention and the necessary steps are immediately taken to restore water quality.

Following routine tests on July 30, Kuressaare Water Utility started chlorinating the water supply after preliminary lab results found E. coli and coliform bacteria at pipeline ends, though official results are pending. Residents in the Upa area are advised to boil drinking water as a precaution, and while the utility notes that coliforms can appear during warm weather due to stagnant water, the first E. coli detection in three years requires immediate action—though it does not indicate widespread contamination.

The source of another E. coli contamination in Saue Municipality near Tallinn remains unknown as authorities conduct joint investigations, though public water is unaffected while private borewell water in the suspected zone is unsafe. Nearly 40 wastewater systems have been inspected — many substandard — but no cause has been confirmed, and construction is also being probed. With spread hard to track, more samples are being taken, and fresh drinking water tanks are available to affected residents.

E.Coli outbreaks were also found in Kuressaare in 2023.

World.title: Iraqi judiciary completes interrogation of 5,700 ISIS suspects
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Supreme Judicial Council of Iraq has officially concluded the interrogation process for 5,704 ISIS detainees who were moved from northeastern Syria earlier this year, preparing them for trial.

The First Karkh Investigation Court said in a statement on Tuesday that it concluded the investigation phase of one of Iraq’s largest terrorism-related cases in history.

The verified detainees originate from 67 different nationalities, including 3,497 Syrians and 474 Iraqis.

The courts identified very dangerous agents in key leadership, military, financial, media, and security roles inside ISIS.

Six offenders were actively linked to the captivity, detention, transfer, sale, and exploitation of Yazidi women, exposing serious international crimes.

Several suspects have previously been cleared and released due to insufficient evidence linking them to terrorism crimes.

In 2014, the terrorist group ISIS took control of large areas in Iraq and Syria before being defeated in 2017.

Over five million Iraqis had to flee the governorates of Nineveh, Salah al-Din, parts of Kirkuk, Diyala, and Anbar because of ISIS control over these areas in 2014.

Although Iraq declared in late 2017 that all of its regions were free of ISIS, the government continues to conduct security operations to hunt out any remaining members of the terrorist group.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate rises in Baghdad, remain stable in Erbil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar rose on Thursday in Baghdad, the Iraqi capital, and remained stable in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,547.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,546.5 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad rose, ranging between 1,552.5 Iraqi dinars and 1,542.5 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate remained stable, fluctuating between 1,546 and 1,545.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation represented more than a 10 percent difference in exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq exports fuel oil through Jordan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told Attaqa News that Iraq began exporting fuel oil shipments via Jordan for the first time last month.

Al-Rikabi explained that Iraq is exporting fuel oil through the neighboring country, not to Jordan.

The Iraqi official did not disclose the details of the agreement, its duration, or when it came into effect.

Iraqi oil shipments started flowing to Jordan in early August through the Trebil border crossing, the only land border crossing between the two countries, at a rate of 10,000 barrels per day, which were stored in the facilities of the Jordan Oil Terminals Company (JOTC), Jordan’s state-owned petroleum logistics and independent storage provider.

Through Jordan, a shipment totaling 307,000 barrels was exported to Greece.

Following the Strait of Hormuz crisis, which began with the United States’ war against Iran on February 28, Iraqi fuel oil shipments began transiting through Syria via tanker trucks, with storage at the Baniyas refinery before shipping to worldwide markets.

Between March and the end of August, Iraq exported 21.4 million barrels of fuel oil through Syria and only 307,000 barrels through Jordan.

Iraqi fuel oil exports started to increase following the Middle East conflict until the end of August in an attempt to compensate for the declining supplies via the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: 38 officers, 3,000 personnel dismissed over corruption in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Interior announced on Thursday that it permanently dismissed 38 officers and 180 personnel over administrative and financial corruption, with another 3,245 personnel discharged for desertion.

The purge represents a significant internal effort as part of the ongoing “Operation Dawn,” a nationwide anti-corruption campaign spearheaded by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government. The campaign has targeted numerous public officials and high-profile individuals.

According to an official statement from Miqdad Miri, the spokesperson for the Interior Ministry, the total number of individuals affected encompasses various categories of misconduct.

After receiving clear evidence of their direct involvement in bribery and financial misconduct, 38 officers were permanently removed from service.

Finalized judicial verdicts convicting 180 enlisted personnel of corruption accusations resulted in their official removal from service.

As part of larger ministry attempts to reestablish strong institutional discipline, 3,245 service personnel were discharged only for abandoning their duties.

These dismissals took place within the first 100 days of the current government’s tenure.

This security-sector cleanup is part of the larger nationwide drive “Operation Dawn.” Between late June and August, security operations resulted in the arrest of at least 210 lawmakers, public servants, and business executives.

World.title: Iraq, AIIB discuss financing development projects
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Finance Minister Faleh Sari met with a delegation from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) led by Konstantin Limitovskiy on Wednesday to discuss funding infrastructure and development projects in Iraq.

During their meeting in Baghdad, the AIIB delegation reviewed its global and regional portfolios to outline how its framework will apply to Iraq across the transportation, energy, water, and digital infrastructure sectors, according to a statement cited by the Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The discussions focused on the Development Road Project, Iraq’s mega-highway and rail corridor intended to connect the Gulf to Europe.

The AIIB publicly stated its willingness to fund and assist this important trans-regional corridor, acknowledging its enormous potential to drive economic diversification.

The Iraqi Ministry of Transport held separate discussions with the World Bank and the AIIB to determine the technological integrations necessary for the project’s ports and rail networks.

The AIIB delegation expressed its willingness to assist and fund important projects in Iraq, particularly major infrastructure projects, such as the Development Road project, which would boost the country’s economic development.

World.title: Iraq launches plan to recover 100,000 artifacts smuggled abroad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has launched a comprehensive plan to recover over 100,000 artifacts that were unearthed through illegal excavation and smuggled out of the country.

The Iraqi Ministry of Culture, Tourism, and Antiquities announced a broad endeavor to recover the country’s stolen Mesopotamian heritage using a combination of cultural diplomacy, security surveillance, and strong legal action.

The ministry’s undersecretary, Qasim al-Sudani, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the government’s agenda prioritizes the tourism sector.

The strategy emphasizes recovering documented items that were assigned official museum inventory numbers prior to their theft and smuggling, especially during the tumultuous period following the 2003 US-led invasion.

The initiative also seeks to tackle the significant number of unrecorded artifacts found during illegal and random excavations.

Since these items lack formal records, they pose a substantially more difficult legal issue to monitor and authenticate.

The Iraqi government has formed a combined domestic task force comprising the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Interior, the National Intelligence Service, and the National Security Service to carry out the plan.

Security agencies are cooperating with Iraqi embassies to identify stolen treasures that appear at public or private auctions abroad.

While countries like the United Kingdom and the United States have actively assisted in the return of tens of thousands of artifacts, Iraqi officials have indicated that some nations have intentionally delayed the repatriation process.

Iraq is also taking legal actions internationally against foreign businesses or individuals who are keeping Iraqi artifacts.

World.title: Iraq evaluates exploration blocks to optimize gas output
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil is actively assessing its exploration blocks and foreign alliances to maximize domestic gas output.

Director of the state-owned Midland Oil Company (MOC), Mohammed Yassin Hassan, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the ministry is focusing on unexploited exploration areas rather than existing resources.

The strategic measure seeks to attract multinational corporations to invest in Iraq’s growing natural gas sector.

Instead of altering production at current sites, the Oil Ministry is focusing on new exploration regions to identify new deposits.

Due to the strong interest in Iraq’s untapped energy potential, multinational energy businesses have already begun contacting the ministry.

Iraq’s MOC is actively pursuing partnerships with major US firms, such as ConocoPhillips, to lead gas development projects in important areas in the provinces of Diyala and Anbar.

Expanding operations in blocks such as the Akkas and Mansuriya gas fields is critical to Iraq’s long-term strategy for achieving energy independence and providing the necessary fuel for power plants to generate electricity.

World.title: Marsoumi: Iraq’s 10M bpd oil goal faces $75B cost and OPEC+ hurdles
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s strategic plan to scale crude oil production to 10 million barrels per day (bpd) by 2030 faces formidable structural, financial, and geopolitical hurdles, prominent Iraqi economic analyst Dr. Nabil Al-Marsoumi warned on Wednesday, September 2, 2026.

The assessment follows directives issued on Tuesday by Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi, who instructed the Ministry of Oil to expand exploration licensing rounds and ramp up extraction across fields in federal territory and the Kurdistan Region to target nearly 10 million bpd over the next four years.

Al-Marsoumi outlined four primary structural constraints standing between Iraq’s current production baseline and the 10-million-bpd horizon:

OPEC+ Baseline & Quota Negotiation: Iraq currently produces approximately 4.431 million bpd against an OPEC+ baseline allocation of 4.651 million bpd. Pushing production toward 10 million bpd requires formal revision of Iraq’s sovereign quota—a concession requiring consensus among major OPEC+ members.

Sustainable Capacity Ceiling: US petroleum consultancy DeGolyer and MacNaughton is actively auditing the maximum sustainable capacity across 19 OPEC+ nations. Preliminary assessments project Iraq’s sustainable 12-month ceiling at 5.0 to 5.5 million bpd, revealing a 4.5-million-bpd capacity deficit below the 2030 target.

Capital Expenditure Threshold ($75 Billion): Based on global industry benchmarks averaging $15 billion in capital investment per 1 million bpd of added capacity, Iraq must mobilize roughly $75 billion in upstream and midstream funding. This capital must finance seawater treatment and injection facilities, storage farm expansions, pumping stations, and new maritime and northern pipeline export corridors.

Price Collapse & Market Saturation Risks: Global oil absorption capacity remains constrained by demand growth projections. Injecting millions of additional Iraqi barrels risks igniting a market-share price war among producers, which could trigger a global oil price collapse harmful to Baghdad’s hydrocarbon-dependent treasury.

Comparative Analysis: Current Capacity vs. 2030 Target

Metric / Parameter Current Level (2026) 2030 Government Target Gap / Required Expansion Crude Output ~4.431 Million bpd 10.000 Million bpd +5.569 Million bpd Sustainable Ceiling 5.0 – 5.5 Million bpd 10.000 Million bpd +4.500 Million bpd OPEC+ Production Baseline 4.651 Million bpd Revised Allocation Required Requires OPEC+ Consensus Estimated Capital Outlay Baseline operational budget ~$75 Billion cumulative $15B per 1M bpd capacity Export Infrastructure Constrained southern/northern routes New northern & deepwater sea lines Major pipeline & storage expansion

Al-Marsoumi cautioned that upstream expansion cannot occur in isolation from global energy market fundamentals. Without substantial foreign direct investment to finance water injection schemes and deepwater export berths, aggressive target-setting risks outpacing actual midstream logistics.

Furthermore, aggressively pursuing volume over price discipline could depress international crude benchmarks, reducing net state oil revenues even as export volumes increase.

World.title: Air India Phuket-Delhi incident: All 3 hydraulic systems failed; pilot tested positive for psychoactive substance
World.content:
The report does not establish that the substance caused the aircraft's sudden loss of altitude. However, the finding puts the pilot's test result under scrutiny as investigators examine the circumstances surrounding the incident.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: The preliminary investigation into the August 4 Air India Phuket-Delhi accident has found that the aircraft's three hydraulic systems, green, blue and yellow, lost pressure within seconds while the A320 was cruising at 36,000 feet, triggering an autopilot disengagement, stall warning and an altitude upset. Alongside the technical findings, the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has recommended that the DGCA take action against the Pilot-in-Command, who tested non-negative for psychoactive substance use following the flight."The confirmation of use of psycho-active substance is a serious concern, and AAIB recommends appropriate actions by DGCA on priority," the report said. The interim safety recommendation asked the regulator to "take appropriate actions as deemed fit to prevent abuse of psycho-active substance." Post-flight, both pilots underwent a breath analyser test, which came back satisfactory. But the subsequent psychoactive substance detection test returned a non-negative result for the PIC, a finding confirmed by a follow-up laboratory blood test. The co-pilot tested negative on both counts.The hydraulic failure itself, the more immediate cause of the injuries onboard, unfolded within a five-second window.VT-EXO, an eight-year-old A320neo carrying 145 people, had just been cleared to climb from FL340 to FL360 after entering Kolkata Flight Information Region. At 04:02:43 UTC, the flight control system "detected loss of green hydraulic system." Four seconds later, the flight control (F/CTL) system detected loss of Blue and Yellow hydraulic systems. With all three systems compromised simultaneously, the autopilot disengaged, a continuous repetitive chime sounded, and the stall warning triggered for two seconds. The aircraft "encountered altitude upset," gaining 372 feet before falling 292 feet from its assigned level, the report said.The co-pilot, who was Pilot Flying, responded first to the upset before the captain took over the controls. Recovery was swift. "At around 04:02:52 UTC, the Blue hydraulic system was recovered, and a few seconds later, the Yellow hydraulic and the Green hydraulic systems were also recovered," the report said. It restored normal flight control surfaces within seconds of the failure.But with seatbelt signs off during cruise, the sudden upset threw passengers and crew around the cabin. Twenty-four people, including four cabin crew, needed medical attention on landing; four were hospitalised with serious injuries. The cabin damage was extensive: cracked ceiling panels across multiple rows, dislodged overhead bins, a broken emergency exit handle, a lavatory commode "uprooted from its original location," and a bent crew seat. Despite the injuries, the flight crew chose not to divert, opting instead to continue to Delhi while requesting medical priority from ATC. The aircraft landed safely on runway 11L at 05:30 UTC, around ninety minutes after the failure.Investigators have already flagged one detail for closer scrutiny: the aircraft was dispatched from Phuket under an active Minimum Equipment List item for the Power Transfer Unit, invoked a week earlier on July 28. The PTU serves as an auxiliary hydraulic source shared between the green and yellow systems, and its status at the time of the failure is expected to be a focus of the ongoing probe. Flight recorder data has been downloaded and is under analysis, and a technical team from Airbus and France's BEA inspected the aircraft in Delhi in mid-August, after which hydraulic components and fluid samples were removed for further testing.âThe Airbus A320 aircraft has three hydraulic systems. They are identified as the green, blue and yellow systems. Together they supply hydraulic power at 3000 psi (206 bar) to the main power users. Services which are not used during flight are isolated from the main supply. Hydraulic fluid cannot be transferred from one system to another. Each system has its own hydraulic reservoir,â the report said, explaining the hydraulics on the aircraft.On the green system, the normal source of pressure is the Engine Driven Pump (EDP) located on the left engine and, as an auxiliary source, the Power Transfer Unit (PTU). On the blue system, the normal source of pressure is the electrical pump (E-Pump) and, as an auxiliary source, the Ram Air Turbine (RAT). On the yellow system, the normal source of pressure is the EDP located on the right engine and as auxiliary sources the PTU and the electric pump (E-Pump). âEach hydraulic system pressurisation information is available for the aircraft systems through one pressure transmitter (numerical value of the pressure), two pressure switches (discrete value indicating if there is a loss of pressure). Relevant Hydraulic components were removed from the aircraft for further analysis,â the report said. The PTU is an auxiliary pressure supply for either the green or yellow systems without transfer of fluid between the two systems. It operates automatically if there is a delta pressure of 500 psi between the green/yellow or yellow/green hydraulic systems, it addedThe said report is preliminary, and a detailed technical investigation is still underway.

World.title: Smoking raises death risk by 55% in people with diabetes, global experts call for active quit treatment
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Smoking increased the risk of death from any cause by 55% among people with diabetes, according to evidence reviewed in a new international consensus that calls for smoking cessation to be treated as an essential part of type 2 diabetes care.

The experts say patients who smoke should be offered medicines, intensive behavioural counselling and regular follow-up instead of being given a one-time âquit smokingâ warning.

The recommendations, published in Diabetes Research and Clinical Practice, are the first dedicated international consensus on smoking cessation specifically for people with type 2 diabetes. They were developed by 35 experts from 13 countries, including Indian diabetes specialist Dr Anoop Misra.

The consensus recommends varenicline as the first-line medicine where available, with nicotine replacement therapy or bupropion as alternatives when varenicline is unavailable or unsuitable. Medicines should be combined with structured, intensive behavioural support and repeated contact rather than brief counselling alone.

The stronger approach reflects the added risk smoking poses in diabetes. A meta-analysis of 48 studies involving 1.13 million people found a 55% higher risk of death, while another study of about 130,000 people with diabetes found 48% higher overall mortality and 36% higher cardiovascular mortality among smokers.





Doctors should review patients within two weeks of quitting and again at four weeks, checking blood sugar, weight, blood pressure and medicines, as quitting can alter drug metabolism and sometimes require dose adjustments.

Weight gain, a common concern, should not deter quitting. In a US cohort of 10,809 people with type 2 diabetes, median weight gain within six years of quitting was 3.2 kg. Long-term quitters had lower all-cause mortality than continuing smokers regardless of weight gain, with mortality hazard ratios of 0.69, 0.57 and 0.51 for no gain, up to 5 kg and more than 5 kg gain, respectively.

Smoking is also linked to kidney damage in diabetes, with higher risks of albuminuria and diabetic nephropathy. A Japanese study of 2,490 people with type 2 diabetes found insulin resistance rose with cigarettes smoked per day and fell with time after quitting.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Quitting, however, can be difficult. Some patients may not recognise the link between smoking and diabetes complications, while others fear weight gain or use cigarettes to cope with stress and anxiety.

The experts recommend personalised quit strategies and relapse prevention.

The consensus also highlights gaps in diabetes care, where smoking cessation often remains limited to brief advice. It calls for routine smoking assessment, active treatment, metabolic monitoring and relapse prevention as part of diabetes care.

World.title: From typewriters to podcasts: the decades that changed the reporter’s worklife, quality of output
World.content:
There was a time when reporting began with being there. A reporter had to physically attend a meeting, listen to the speaker, collect the press note and, more importantly, observe what happened around the event. The words spoken at the microphone were only one part of the story. The conversations before and after the meeting often provided the real information.

The newsroom, meanwhile, operated at a distinctly different pace. Copies were typed on typewriters. The reporter’s typed sheets were then handed over to operators who fed them into the newly introduced computers. A mistake meant the familiar ritual of striking out a word, retyping it or starting again.

Then came the early word-processing systems. The introduction of software such as MSSoft was liberating for reporters. For the first time, many could write their copies directly on a computer. Wrong spellings could be erased and rewritten without the clutter of corrections on paper.

It was a small technological change, but it felt revolutionary. English-language reporters were the envy of many vernacular reporters who continued to work with more cumbersome processes.

For a long time, the lone landline telephone in the office was the lifeline. Those wanting to give information and those seeking it had to wait for their turn. Reporters took slots to use the phone. Fax machines brought another change. They buzzed incessantly and consumed enormous quantities of paper, receiving press notes from anywhere.

Then came the pager. Compared with today’s smartphones, the pager was a primitive device, yet it revolutionised the way reporters received information. Messages were short and crisp: “Rush to press conference.” “Check accident.” “Call office.”

When The Hindu became one of the first newspapers in Hyderabad to use the technology, possessing one was something of a status symbol among reporters.

I still remember how information about the infamous Jubilee Hills bomb blast, targeting then TDP Minister Paritala Ravi, was conveyed to a colleague through a pager. The pager’s arrival marked an important change - the reporter no longer had to be at the office to receive instructions.

The mobile phone took that transformation several steps further.

When the first mobile phones began appearing in the late 1990s, they were scarce and the privilege largely belonged to the bosses. The ability to reach a journalist anytime, anywhere, was itself a new phenomenon.

Once mobile phones became available to reporters, the traditional boundaries of the working day began to disappear. Journalism became a 24-hour profession.

Emails added another dimension. Reporters could receive large volumes of material instantaneously. Unlike paper, emails could be stored, searched and retrieved. Information that might earlier have disappeared into a pile of files could now be preserved for years.

But the greatest transformation came with the smartphone and messaging applications. The smartphone changed the very definition of being a reporter.

Technology was expected to make journalism easier. In some ways, it did. A reporter could access documents, make calls, record interviews, take photographs, check facts and file a story from a single device.

But the paradox was that the easier the tools became, the longer the working day became. The reporter now has to file a story from home, while having a meal at a restaurant, or even during a morning walk. News no longer waited for the reporter to reach the office. The office, effectively, travelled with the reporter.

Today, news is consumed on the move. A reporter is expected not only to follow the news but to anticipate it, react to it, update it and, often, explain it almost immediately. Now the role extends far beyond filing a written story. They are increasingly expected to visually tell the story through videos and add value with related podcasts. The reporter is expected to master newer technologies covering digital narrations in line with the changing preferences of the audience. The reporter is now chronicler of instant history using all formats.

Yet, for all the advantages of technology, something has been lost. The long conversations over tea and snacks, picking up information that would never have appeared in an official statement. A press note arrives.

The reporter reads it. Perhaps a call follows. The story is filed. The next message arrives. The typewriter disappeared. The landline became redundant. The fax machine is in a bin. The pager vanished. Even the desktop computer has surrendered much of its importance to the smartphone.

Somewhere between the typewriter and WhatsApp, we lost the time required to build the relationships that once made reporting richer.

(ravikanth.ramasayam@thehindu.co.in)
