World.title: Decades of capturing history one frame at a time
World.content:
Long before digital sensors and instant cloud uploads revolutionized the Press, capturing history for The Hindu across undivided Andhra Pradesh was an endurance sport.

It was defined by the pungent smell of darkroom chemicals in dimly lit hotel rooms, tight deadlines, and an unyielding commitment to truth, recalls former Chief News Photographer H. Satish.

From the quiet beginnings of the Hyderabad edition in 1976 — when senior journalists relied on State public relations photos and freelance shots — the newspaper’s visual narrative shifted radically in 1990.

The department was started by photo editor S. Kodandaraman who came from then Madras with two cameras and handed them over to Mr. H. Satish. The number of photographers gradually increased over the years as the city edition got prominence with more pages. It was an opportunity for the staff photojournalists to transform the city and regional reportage capturing the pivotal political moments, changes in the city landscapes, the quiet rhythm of daily life and human tragedies, among others.

Whether in documenting the aftermath of the Latur earthquake, exposing raw human realities like child labour, or filing breaking images amidst citywide curfews, naxalite shoot-outs, the visual team anchored the newsroom.

Field reporting in the pre-digital era demanded raw physical grit. Photojournalists navigated assignments carrying darkroom kits into makeshift hotel setups. They processed negatives manually, rushing against time to transmit images via standalone fax machines over single telephone lines – often sending the solitary photograph that would inform the nation the next morning.

During moments of extreme crisis, like the catastrophic 2005 Valigonda train collision, photojournalists rode two-wheelers through flooded terrain, joining rescue operations while securing historic visual evidence under torrential rains. The team had noted news photographers like P.V. Sivakumar, S. Gajendran, Mohd. Yousuf, K. Ramesh Babu and others who served the organisation for years with aplomb.

Even as the cameras got transformed into SLRs followed by the digital cameras, the photojournalists got an additional job of shooting videos and within no time, our team has been straddling both still photos and videography for the print/digital editions. We are now a three-member strong team, including G. Ramakrishna, a relatively younger Siddhanth Thakur and stringer photographer Mohd. Arif shooting from Sangareddy.

(nagara.gopal@thehindu.co.in)

World.title: Uttar Pradesh floods: Over 17,500 evacuated, 26 districts hit
World.content:
More than 17,500 people have been evacuated to safer places from 26 flood-affected areas in Uttar Pradesh, with no loss of life or livestock reported so far, the state government said on Friday.

According to the office of the Relief Commissioner, around 3.53 lakh people have been affected by the floods. As many as 17,544 people have been moved to safer locations, while 4,847 people are currently staying in relief shelters.

A total of 1,312 flood shelters have been set up across the state, while 1,634 flood outposts, 1,697 boats and motorboats and 1,068 medical teams have been deployed in the affected areas, the government said in a statement issued on Friday.

The relief machinery has distributed 72,897 food relief packets and 3,67,551 lunch packets among affected people. More than 5.52 lakh chlorine tablets and 1.87 lakh ORS packets have also been distributed as part of health and sanitation measures.

More than 5,000 quintals of fodder have been provided for livestock. Over 45,000 animals have been affected by the floods, but no livestock death has been reported, the statement said.

The affected districts are Amroha, Ayodhya, Azamgarh, Badaun, Ballia, Barabanki, Basti, Chandauli, Farrukhabad, Ghazipur, Gonda, Gorakhpur, Hardoi, Kasganj, Kanpur, Lakhimpur Kheri, Mirzapur, Moradabad, Pilibhit, Prayagraj, Raebareli, Rampur, Sant Kabir Nagar, Shahjahanpur, Unnao and Varanasi.

In Chitrakoot, the water level of the Mandakini River has receded to 128 metres from its peak of 135.20 metres recorded on August 29, but authorities continue to monitor the situation and relief operations, the government said.

As many as 688 people have been evacuated to safer locations, while 13,906 people in 36 affected villages have received assistance.

The affected areas include 19 villages in Karwi, seven in Rajapur and 10 in Manikpur.

The administration has distributed 28,803 lunch packets and 2,065 relief kits in the affected areas. Eighteen flood shelters are operational, while 28 medical teams equipped with ambulances and medicines have been deployed.

The government said 653 houses suffered partial damage in the floods. Financial assistance of Rs 7.52 lakh has been transferred to the accounts of 188 affected beneficiaries, while Rs 1.20 lakh has been provided in a case of complete damage. Payments in other cases are being processed.

A 30-member National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) team and two State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams comprising 27 personnel have also been deployed in the district. Authorities are conducting crop-loss surveys to assess damage to farmers.

In Ghazipur, police and the administration rescued 12 shepherds and more than 2,000 sheep stranded on an island near Duhia Saraiya as the Ganga River's water level rose.

The rescue operation lasted around six hours. A joint police-administration team reached Dadri Ghat after receiving information late at night and used a night-vision drone to locate the stranded people and animals.

The PAC flood company, police, administrative teams and local boatmen then carried out the rescue operation, in which there was no loss of life, the statement said.

World.title: Jadavpur University students use ex-PM Vajpayee’s remark to justify ‘Free Palestine’ graffiti
World.content:
Students of Jadavpur University on Thursday (September 3, 2026) put up a poster in the campus of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee’s remark on the territorial integrity of Palestine.

Only a day before, the administration whitewashed all the graffiti from the walls of the university after Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari directed the university administration to take action against the ‘anti-national’ graffiti painted on the walls, including the ones demanding freedom of Palestine and Kashmir, and also slogans on shooting the fascists.

The poster of the former Prime Minister was put up at the green zone area of the university, in which the ex-PM said, “Israel must return the lands of Arabs it has occupied. The lawful rights of the Palestinians must be established.”

The statement was made by Mr. Vajpayee in 1977 at a public meeting in Delhi shortly after the Janata Party government came to power for the first time. He was then given the charge of the External Affairs Ministry.

At the bottom of the poster, credit was given to the “nationalist students of Jadavpur University”. A QR code linked to Mr. Vajpayee’s full speech was also included in the poster.

After the State CM’s directive on August 26, 2026, the university administration whitewashed all the graffiti across the main building, Aurobindo Bhaban, the Arts Hostel, and the Open-Air Theatre. However, the graffiti was repainted, which students claimed was an attempt to ‘reclaim’ the walls of the university.

One of the freshly painted graffiti on Monday (August 31, 2026) quoted Karl Marx, saying, “We have no compassion, and we ask no compassion from you. When our turn comes, we shall not make excuses for the terror.”

A day later, a group of police personnel and officials from the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) arrived at the university at around 12:30 a.m. on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) and whitewashed all the graffiti on the walls of the JU campus. This included a portrait of artist Chittaprosad Bhattacharya, a painting on climate change, as well as the aforementioned statement of Marx, quotes from Ho Chi Minh, Urdu couplets, and more.

However, the graffiti and the poster were back on the walls across the campus once again on Thursday (September 3, 2026).

Apart from the former PM’s poster, a sarcastic graffiti on Italian dictator Benito Mussolini and the RSS was also painted to justify the ‘Azadi’ slogan, which was also termed as ‘anti-national’. This graffiti said, “Mussolini ko de di Azadi, RSS ko bhi de denge Azadi” (Mussolini was given freedom, so will be given to RSS as well).

A few more sarcastic graffiti on Vinayak Damodar Savarkar was also seen on Thursday (September 3, 2026).

To counter the graffiti and posters by the Left students, the ABVP also put up photos and posters on Rabindranath Tagore, Vidyasagar, Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay and Vande Mataram across the campus on Thursday (September 3, 2026).

However, on Thursday (September 3, 2026), the State CM further launched a scathing attack on the dissident voices within the university.

“Bengal is the land of Netaji and Shyamaprasad. Swami Vivekananda was born in Kolkata. And on this land you will say ‘Kashmir maange azaadi’! There are no rallies when Pahalgam happens, but during Operation Sindoor, you say, Stop the war. Do we have to tolerate these things? You will write ‘Free Palestine’ on the walls of Jadavpur? Write ‘Free PoK’. I will support it,” he said, addressing the annual programme of Vivekananda Vidya Bharati Vikas Parishad, an RSS-affiliated organisation, at Ramakrishna Mission in Kolkata’s Golpark.

Rallies by ABVP and Left students

Meanwhile, the Left students took out a rally against the invitation of several BJP leaders, including Rahul Sinha, Swapan Dasgupta, and Tapas Roy, and also the Jadavpur MLA Sarbori Mukherjee at a ‘Nationalist Conference’ that took place at the Triguna Sen auditorium in the university. The event was organised by an organisation, Haripada Bharati Smritiraksha Samiti, in the afternoon.

The students opposed the invitation of the BJP leaders inside the campus days after the clash erupted between the ABVP and Left students on August 20.

Jadavpur University had emerged as the flashpoint of the right versus left politics after a group of Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad Supporters forced themselves inside the university premises on August 19 and tried to tear posters and burn flags of the left student’s union. The university has been on the boil since then.

“Ms. Mukherjee sent outsiders inside the campus who vandalised the university and set fire to the main building late at night. Why was she invited?,” asked the general secretary of the Students’ Federation of India, Srijan Bhattacharya, during the protest rally at 8B Bus Stand opposite to the University.

He also added that the graffiti made by the students reflects the opinions of the public. “CM cannot decide which one of them is nationalist and anti-nationalist. If he thinks those are not the opinions of the common people, why doesn’t he conduct the students’ union election and let the students decide it through voting?”

The ABVP supporters also held another rally inside the campus, carrying the national flag and uttering ‘Vande Mataram’.

Calling the left students spoiling the environment of the university, they said that they have been pushing an anti-national mentality and don’t allow any other voices to be raised democratically.

World.title: Fishing trip turns 22-day saga of survival
World.content:
When 49-year-old Koppanathi Ramakrishna set sail into the Bay of Bengal at around 9 a.m. on August 3, 2026, he expected to return in a fortnight with a boatload of tuna, in particular yellowfin tuna (Thunnus albacares). Instead, his maiden deep-sea fishing voyage turned into a 22-day ordeal, leaving him and his six-member crew adrift hundreds of nautical miles from home, with dwindling food and supplies and no way to contact their families.

The journey had begun with hope and careful planning. Ramakrishna, who had only fished in the waters of the Vynateya, a branch of the Godavari River that meets with the Bay of Bengal at Komaragiripatnam in Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district, was determined to venture into the deep-sea to catch the tuna, one of the most prized oceanic fisheries resource.

Born into a fisherfolk family, the 49-year-old fisherman was well-equipped with the river and its fishing diversity. But, he had never sailed into the deep sea for fishing. His quest for the deep-sea fishing came at a time when the country was experiencing high exports of tuna. India exported 51,626 tonnes of tuna in 2023-24, worth $87.96 million, an increase of 31.83% from the previous year, according to the Marine Products Export Development Authority. (Source: https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/centre-aims-to-make-andaman-nicobar-islands-a-tuna-export-hub/article68878943.ece)

It was against this backdrop that Ramakrishna decided to venture into the deep sea. He met with the community priest, shared his quest for a voyage, and sought an auspicious time for the sail on his own mechanised boat (IND-AP-E8-MO-135). The boat also carried this faith, as it was painted yellow, representing turmeric, which fisherfolk throw into the sea at the beginning of the annual fishing season on July 14 as part of an auspicious ritual.

Alongside ritualistic preparations, Ramakrishna had also taken practical precautions for his sail. He collected a transponder from the local Fisheries Department for his boat. The Government of Andhra Pradesh supplies transponders free of cost for installation on registered fishing boats. These satellite-connected communication devices share the boat’s location with the government and allows the crew to send alerts in an event of emergency.

“I was slightly hesitant to install the transponder on my boat. However, as the auspicious time and date approached for our voyage, our seven-member crew set sail at around 9 a.m. on August 3 from the Odalarevu fish landing point and entered the sea after crossing the calm waters of Vynateya in less than an hour,” says Ramakrishna.

Just like Ramakrishna, the journey was also a first for another crew member, Palepu Santa Rao, who speaks Hindi. This deep-sea fishing expedition was his maiden voyage. The designated boat drivers were 60-year-old Sangani Tata Rao from Brahma Samedhyam and 37-year-old Kollati Srinubabu from Odalarevu. The remaining crew members included Karri Rambabu from Komaragiripatnam, Kollati Yesudasu from Bendamuru Lanka village, and Kataadi Satish Kumar from Pasuvullanka. Led by Ramakrishna, they formed a seven-member crew.

The seven men prepared for a fortnight at the sea. The boat was laden with four tonnes of ice meant for storing tuna, 1,000 litres of diesel, two tonnes of water for drinking, cooking, and bathing, and commodities — rice, oil, and spices — sufficient for 15 days.

“We had three cell phones on board; mine was the most valuable because I had stored notes on locations, including latitude and longitude—beginning from Visakhapatnam to Odisha, Paradeep, and the West Bengal coasts—as a precaution,” says Ramakrishna. He reveals that these notes were shared by an expert driver from Kakinada to help them understand and navigate the nearby coast when matched with the boat’s GPS system.

According to the plan

For a while, the voyage unfolded as planned. The crew enjoyed their first two meals on the boat on August 3. Slowly, the blue waters became invisible as darkness fell. They sailed nearly 35 nautical miles without casting their nets, uncertain about the catch. The first two nights of the voyage passed without even attempting to cast the net. Equipped with a gill net, they tried to target tuna during the night. However, the fish they had travelled so far to catch remained elusive, and on the third day, they noticed that something was wrong.

“On August 5, the third night, we tried our luck for three hours until midnight, casting nets nearly 60 nautical miles parallel to our native coast. But the tuna remained elusive. Suddenly, we noticed an unusual sound from the clutch plates, causing the boat engine to fall silent,” says Palepu Santa Rao from Odalarevu village. By then, not a single school of tuna had been caught. On the same day, they contacted their families for the last time before proceeding further.

Without the engine, the crew could no longer control their course. Santa Rao says, “The next day, we flagged ‘therachapa’ (canvas) to navigate the boat towards the coast, following the wind direction and avoiding any threat of the boat overturning in the sea.”

Fear and survival

By August 7, the boat had been driven by the winds nearly 200 nautical miles away from the Visakhapatnam coast. “In the deep sea, we stopped fishing because we were scared of the giant fish species. We saw one giant fish, believed to be a whale, that came close to our boat. It could have overturned our boat. We were frightened to see the size of the creatures found in the sea,” recall Ramakrishna and the driver, Srinubabu.

While the seven men struggled to keep the boat moving, life continued as usual for their families back home. Santa Rao’s family, including his wife Nagalakshmi and sister Sarada, was busy with their everyday chores. Srinubabu, a father of two children studying in Classes VII and IV, hoped for the crew to return home by August 13 or 14 as scheduled.

With rescue nowhere in sight, Ramakrishna realised that keeping his crew hopeful was as important as feeding them. For the next week, Ramakrishna continued to instil hope in his crew members. “I remember telling them to trust me while assuring them that we would not die. Something good will surely happen,” recalls Ramakrishna.

Behind those attempts to keep morale up was a constant fear of collision. The crew members kept themselves busy preparing food and sharing tales from their villages while remaining vigilant for any boat or vessel that might pass by. “I did not sleep during the nights; I kept holding the light to signal our presence in the water to avoid being hit by any large vessel,” says Ramakrishna.

Then came a sighting that briefly raised their hopes. At 116 nautical miles away from Paradeep, a defence or Coast Guard chopper flashed a light on their boat during the night. “We thought it was deployed for our rescue. We responded by flashing our light, but they proceeded without making contact. We understood that it was part of their training session,” recalls Ramakrishna.

Days later another sighting offered a glimmer of hope. By August 20, the boat was sighted by two fishing boats close to Astaranga Beach (Puri district in Odisha), nearly 60 km south of Paradeep. “The crew of the two boats spoke to us in Hindi, gave us a helpline number, and then proceeded to go fishing without hearing our ordeal. We could not reach out to that helpline number due to a lack of signals,” says Santa Rao.

Families seek help

Back home, the disappearance of the fishermen had triggered a massive search operation. The families of the seven men contacted District Collector R. Mahesh Kumar and appealed for help. In response to their appeal, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu ordered a massive search operation, after which the Eastern Naval Command and the Indian Coast Guard were deployed to intensify the search, covering up to 300 nautical miles.

State Agriculture Minister and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema District In-Charge Minister K. Atchannaidu assured the families on August 19 that the State government has alerted the administrations and fishing boat associations in Odisha and West Bengal.

At least 15 Coast Guard vessels and four helicopters were deployed; electronic surveillance was conducted by the Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre, and Myanmar and Bangladesh maritime authorities were also put on alert, revealed Mr. Atchannaidu. The Indian Navy and Coast Guard were asked to cover a range of up to 300 nautical miles to trace the fishing boat, he added. India’s Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), where fishing activity is allowed by Indian boats, extends up to 200 nautical miles from the coast.

For those waiting at home, however, the search brought no answers. In Odalarevu, Kameswari, 34, the wife of Kollati Srinubabu, spent her days at the temples of the local deities, praying for the safe return of her husband, while her two boys played on the banks of the Vynateya, unaware of their father’s ordeal.

“Our hope for the survival of the crew faded as we heard no signs of the missing boat. By August 25, the government stated that the operation was ongoing, but there was no progress in tracing the missing boat,” says Ms. Kameswari, whose family lives in a rented house and ekes out a livelihood through fishing in the river.

At sea, meanwhile, the situation for the seven men was becoming increasingly desperate. “All our food stock was gone by August 22. The leftover ice had melted for drinking and cooking, and we barely caught 14 fish, which we boiled before eating,” says Srinubabu. Except for 60-year-old Sangani Tata Rao, who has a history of low blood pressure, none of the crew members suffered any illness, he adds.

‘Wish of God’

After three weeks of uncertainty, help finally found them. On August 26, the boat was sighted by two fishing boats 16 kilometres away from Shankarpur fishing harbour near Digha port in Purba Medinipur in West Bengal.

The crew of one of the two boats rescued the fishermen and offered them food before bringing them to the Shankarpur fishing harbour. Their first priority after reaching the harbour was to contact their families. Ramakrishna called his brother Venkat to inform him of their survival and to spread the word. “I heard my brother Ramakrishna’s voice on a call on August 26 and spread the news like wildfire. I immediately alerted the officials,” says Venkat.

Collector R. Mahesh Kumar says, “Upon being informed about the rescue of our fishermen by West Bengal fisherfolk, we sent a team of officials to bring them back.” The rescued fishermen were kept under the observation of doctors for one day in West Bengal. The entire journey, challenges, survival strategies, sea conditions, and the ordeal of the surviving fishermen have been recorded to formulate a rescue plan to save more lives in the future, the Collector adds.

Back home, their survival prompted both celebration and reflection. The seven fishermen went house to house thanking the families and villagers who prayed for their safe return. Last Sunday, the families of all the survivors offered special prayers to their local deities.

For Ramakrishna, the experience has changed the way he visualises the sea. “My boat is still anchored on the West Bengal coast. If we had not returned, I would have been blamed for the loss of the lives of my crew for the rest of my life,” he says.

The 49-year-old, who has a wife, a daughter and a son, has decided to quit deep-sea fishing. He began his voyage hoping for a boatful of tuna, and instead returned with an experience for a lifetime. “Our survival was the wish of God,” he says.

World.title: HDB region emerging as promising technology, manufacturing, investment corridor: Karnataka Minister Priyank Kharge
World.content:
The Hubballi-Dharwad-Belagavi (HDB) region is emerging as one of Karnataka’s most promising technology, manufacturing, and investment corridors, according to Priyank Kharge, Minister for IT, BT and Home Department.

The HDB region has a strong industrial base and is now seeing growing capabilities in technology, advanced manufacturing, and innovation, he said adding, HDB was building capabilities across semiconductors, Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM), electric vehicles, artificial intelligence, deep tech, Industry 4.0, and advanced engineering.

These three cities bring different strengths to this ecosystem and that offers the region a strong foundation to build a larger technology and manufacturing ecosystem, the Minister stated.

Hubballi has a growing technology and entrepreneurial base; Dharwad has strong academic and research institutions, while Belagavi has an established base in aerospace, precision engineering and advanced manufacturing.

“Bringing these strengths together can create a strong ecosystem for innovation, investment and enterprise,’’ the Minister said on the sidelines of HDB Techceleration 2026 in Hubballi on September 3.

According to a statement from the IT ministry, the response to HDB Techceleration 2026 has been very encouraging. The summit brought together more than 700 delegates, over 100 startups and 25 investors, along with industry, academia and technology stakeholders.

This overwhelming participation was a clear indication of the interest and confidence that is building around HDB and its potential, Mr. Kharge said adding, “This is at the heart of our Beyond Bengaluru vision — to build strong technology and innovation ecosystems across Karnataka and create opportunities closer to where talent, institutions and industry are already present.”

According to the Minister, HDB has many of the ingredients needed to make that vision a reality. “We will make it easier for companies to establish and scale in the region, strengthen innovation and advanced manufacturing, and connect HDB to national and global markets.”

HDB has the industrial base, institutions, and technology capabilities to play a much bigger role in the growth of Karnataka.

“We want to build on these strengths and create an ecosystem where companies can grow, startups can scale, and more high-quality opportunities are created in north Karnataka,” Mr. Kharge said.

World.title: FO says Indian claims about Hindu temple in Narowal 'false, politically motivated'
World.content:
The Foreign Office (FO) on Friday rejected claims made by the Indian Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) regarding a Hindu temple in Narowal as “false and politically motivated”, adding that the neighbouring country was “distorting facts and resorting to cheap gimmicks”.

According to the government, the over-a-century-old temple in Siraj village had collapsed following torrential rains. A minority rights group, however, claimed that the structure was deliberately razed to facilitate the expansion of an adjoining seminary.

Subsequently, the Indian MEA issued a statement calling on the government to conduct a prompt and transparent investigation, condemning what it called a “reprehensible act of vandalism”.

In a statement shared on the social media platform X, FO Spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said Pakistan categorically rejected “the false and politically motivated assertions” made by India regarding the temple in Narowal.

He said, unlike the “false propaganda” being peddled by India, the temple’s structure was damaged on July 21 due to torrential rains.

“The local authorities have already surveyed the rain damage and initiated steps for the restoration of the building,” the spokesperson said.

“It is, therefore, shameful that India is distorting facts and resorting to cheap gimmicks,” he added.

The FO spokesperson said the “deliberate distortion of facts” could not distract attention from India’s “abysmal record of systematic persecution of minorities and state-sponsored attacks against their places of worship”.

“The world is well aware of the weaponisation of Hindutva ideology against minorities, and must hold the Indian leadership accountable for the persecution of Muslim, Sikh and Christian communities,” the FO spokesperson concluded.

World.title: Govt eyes petrol deregulation by June next year
World.content:
• High-speed diesel to be deregulated at a later stage

• Ogra may be empowered to adjust diesel pricing without repeated cabinet approvals

• Petroleum price stabilisation fund unlikely to be operationalised

ISLAMABAD: The government is unlikely to operationalise the recently created Petroleum Prices Stabilisation Fund (PPSF) and instead plans more changes to the pricing mechanism, including complete deregulation of petrol by June 2027, with high-speed diesel to follow at a later stage.

A meeting of the committee on petroleum pricing, led by Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik, also agreed in principle to empower the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) to switch diesel pricing to crude-based calculations in case of an unusual rise in the diesel crack spread without seeking repeated approvals from the federal cabinet.

The cabinet had last month temporarily capped the HSD crack spread — the gap between international diesel and crude oil prices — at $41.89 per barrel after it averaged above $60, resulting in windfall gains for local refineries and sharp increases in their profitability and share prices.

Once approved, Ogra would be able to adjust the HSD crack spread within a prescribed floor-and-cap mechanism.

“For diesel pricing, the committee approved the guiding principles for possible rules-based intervention in case of an emergency situation, with clearly defined price-shock triggers and possible corrective measures,” the petroleum division said in a statement.

Informed sources said the committee agreed that, despite usual hue and cry, daily price adjustments had worked well and generally helped stabilise the market by avoiding the larger shocks associated with longer pricing intervals in the past.

They said this had reduced the need for a price stabilisation fund, which would otherwise require additional taxation for financing.

Sources said a consultancy working on the subject had advised the government that maintaining adequate fuel stocks generally worked better for price stability than intervention through stabilisation funds, which could create price and market distortions.

Therefore, the government intends to proceed in phases, starting with the complete deregulation of petrol pricing — similar to high-octane products such as 97 RON HOBC and 95 RON — with daily adjustments by June 2027.

For consumers, deregulation could mean more frequent changes in petrol prices and, eventually, different prices across oil marketing companies as they compete in the market. It could offer cheaper options in some cases but would also expose consumers more directly to movements in international oil prices and the exchange rate.

In a subsequent phase, diesel pricing would also be considered for complete deregulation, allowing oil marketing companies (OMCs) to adjust prices in a competitive environment.

The petroleum division said the committee had agreed on a set of recommendations to strengthen the existing pricing mechanism and would submit its final report to the prime minister for consideration and approval.

Informed sources said some additional technical input was still required and the process was expected to be concluded in another two or three committee meetings.

The committee also reviewed recommendations on the petrol pricing formula and set a likely June 2027 target for deregulation, with the aim of ensuring a gradual transition towards competitive, market-based pricing while protecting consumers from excessive price volatility.

The meeting reviewed the existing Inland Freight Equalisation Margin (IFEM) mechanism, which is used to maintain uniform depot-stage petroleum prices across the country, and agreed on a revised methodology for calculating it.

Ogra assured the committee that the IFEM audit for FY26 would be completed by the end of calendar year 2026.

The committee also directed Ogra to submit written recommendations on consolidation and performance of existing oil marketing companies, especially in terms of adoption of best practices and latest technologies.

Informed sources said a major player associated with a leading OMC was already absconding after allegedly being found involved in unfair business practices, while the petroleum division wanted its foreign partner to play a greater role in operating retail outlets.

The committee reviewed reports of subcommittees on the proposed price stabilisation fund, benchmarked against various successful and unsuccessful international models, and directed the subgroup to further refine its proposals.

“The committee, however, observed that in view of the ultimate deregulation of the market, maintaining adequate fuel reserves would be more appropriate than establishing a stabilisation fund,” the petroleum division said.

The committee believed the proposed changes would improve predictability and transparency in petroleum pricing, enhance market efficiency and safeguard consumers from abrupt price movements while facilitating a gradual transition towards deregulation.

A subcommittee headed by NetSol’s Naeem Ghauri was also advised to meet Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) Chairman Rashid Langrial to assess whether the taxation regime needed to be reviewed in light of changing market conditions.

The government had notified the establishment of a petroleum price stabilisation fund in June amid sharp price fluctuations following US attacks on Iran. However, the fund currently holds no deposits, although the Ministry of Finance has already created special heads of account for it.

Published in Dawn, September 4th, 2026

World.title: Ex-Pakistan coach Jason Gillespie tells Aaqib Javed to 'look in the mirror' over cricket team sackings
World.content:
Former Pakistan Test coach Jason Gillespie said on Friday chairman of selectors Aaqib Javed needs to “look at himself in the mirror” with the national team “playing with fear”.

In a shock move Pakistan this week replaced head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and pace-bowling chief Umar Gul, and sent seven players home from England, in a dramatic response to successive Test thrashings.

Australia’s Gillespie, who led the side for eight months in 2024, including a 2-1 Test series win against England, said it was sad to see.

“I feel for the players, this is these guys’ livelihoods,” he told The Australian newspaper.*

“From the outside it looks like they are playing with fear.

“Salman Ali Agha goes from captaining the team in the first Test against England to out of the team for the second Test and on the plane home before the third Test,” he said.

“How does that work?” he asked, laying the blame firmly at the door of Javed.

“It’s pretty clear they don’t have a selection strategy at all, particularly under Javed. They change their mind like they change their pants — daily,” he said.

“Javed came out recently and blamed (former white-ball coach) Gary Kirsten and myself for everything that is going on.

“Javed has been chairman of selectors for the past two years. We haven’t even been there,” he said.

“Somehow he claims it is our fault. Make sense out of that. I think Javed needs to look at himself in the mirror,” he added.

The tourists suffered an innings and 103-run loss in the series opener at Headingley before going down by 194 runs at Lord’s.

The third and final Test starts at Edgbaston on September 9.

“There is definitely no communication between Javed, who is meant to be chairman of selectors, and the players,” added Gillespie.

“The players who were sacked heard it through family and friends and the media they had been sacked.

“How disrespectful is that?”

Several other ex-Pakistan coaches and players have been left similarly bewildered, including former captains Shahid Afridi and Shoaib Malik.

Ex-coach Mickey Arthur called it “an absolutely ridiculous situation”.

New Zealander Mike Hesson, who was already Pakistan’s white-ball chief, and Australian Ashley Noffke, have taken charge for the rest of the tour.

World.title: 2 trapped tunnel workers rescued in Nepal more than a week after catastrophic flash floods
World.content:
Two hydropower workers were pulled from a tunnel buried by debris in Nepal on Friday, more than a week after catastrophic flooding swept through the area, government ministers said.

Rescuers cheered as one man was pulled from a muddy opening, video released by the energy ministry showed. He was helped to his feet by rescuers.

A photograph showed the second man caked in mud, his hands pressed together in prayer, as rescuers carried him away on an orange stretcher.

The men were named as Sanjay Shah, 30, a mechanical foreman, and Kabir Maharjan, 45, a mechanical supervisor, by Home Minister Sudan Gurung.

“I am so happy, my heart is lighter,” Amir Maharjan, the brother of rescued worker Kabir Maharjan, told AFP.

The two are among hundreds of hydropower workers missing since a wall of mud and debris swept through the region on August 26.

Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha confirmed that one person had been safely rescued from the Trishuli 3A tunnel, followed shortly afterwards by a second.

“We have just received news that another person … has also been rescued,” Gurung said in a statement.

The government had initially said it believed more than 100 workers could be alive inside multiple tunnels. Searches were continuing at Trishuli 3A and other sites.

‘Back in miracle country’

Rescue teams in Nepal have recovered more than 1,250 bodies, and more than 5,000 are missing, after the gigantic wave triggered by a rock and ice avalanche roared down the China-Nepal border.

Australian rescue expert Arnold Dix, who has advised on multiple tunnel-collapse rescues, has been supporting the operation remotely and is travelling to Nepal to support teams on the ground.

Earlier on Friday, Dix, president of the International Tunnelling and Underground Space Association, said teams at the Trishuli 3A hydropower project believed they had heard a faint response from inside the tunnel.

He said rescuers had called into the tunnel: “Don’t worry, we are rescuing you.”

“They believe they received a faint response from inside saying, ‘hunchha’, yes or OK,” Dix told AFP, adding that he was en route to Nepal to join the rescue effort.

“Right now, I’m ‘glass three-quarters full’… After a week of 24/7 heartache, we might, just, be back in miracle country,” he said.

Dix said teams had dug through debris blocking the tunnel for 50 to 60 metres and had been hoping for a breakthrough at any moment.

Less than an hour later, rescuers pulled the two men to safety.

World.title: Makkah Pact will provide ‘deterrence for peace’
World.content:
• Ahsan Iqbal calls for ‘economic reset’ to sustain strategic achievements

• Ex-foreign minister says alliance safeguards sovereignty of all three states

LAHORE: Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal and Punjab Assembly Speaker Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan on Thursday described the Makkah Pact as an important strategic development, with the minister linking it to Pakistan’s defence and diplomatic gains and the speaker saying it should serve as an instrument for promoting peace through deterrence.

They were speaking at a seminar titled ‘Makkah Pact and New Geometry of Power’, hosted by the University of Lahore.

Mr Iqbal said Pakistan had achieved significant successes on both the defence and diplomatic fronts, but warned that such gains could not be sustained unless the country also strengthened itself economically and put its domestic affairs in order.

“Without economic strength, defence and diplomatic successes begin to lose their effectiveness over time,” the minister said.

Mr Iqbal described Pakistan’s recent defence and diplomatic achievements as historic and remarkable, but said they also placed an equal responsibility on the country to put its internal affairs in order.

“Pakistan now needs to focus completely on its economy,” he said, calling for an “economic reset”.

He said that in a rapidly changing world, the ability to reset and adapt had become essential for survival.

“Even multibillion-dollar companies can face decline if they fail to reinvent themselves,” he said, citing once-dominant technology companies that had failed to adapt to changing times.

“In a changing world, resetting and adapting to new realities is essential for survival,” he added.

Punjab Assembly Speaker Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan said he hoped the pact would serve as an instrument for promoting peace in the region through deterrence.

He said the agreement conveyed a message of strength and unity among Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.

Former foreign minister Khurshid Mahmood Kasuri said the Makkah Pact reflected the sentiments of the wider Muslim world and ordinary people in Cairo, Jeddah, Lahore, Karachi, Ankara and Istanbul.

He described it as a deterrence arrangement aimed at safeguarding the integrity and sovereignty of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.

Former national security adviser Nasir Janjua said the global balance of power was shifting, with the influence of Russia, China and the Muslim world rising against a “relative decline of the United States”. He called for greater regional unity as a basis for stability.

Former foreign secretary Jalil Abbas Jilani said the pact reflected Pakistan’s diplomatic achievements and should be viewed in the context of the evolving strategic environment in the Middle East.

University of Lahore Chairman Awais Raoof said the erosion of the global order and human rights in recent years had made the emergence of the Makkah Pact a welcome development for the region.

He said universities had a responsibility to provide a platform for debate on such issues.

Mr Raoof described the agreement as defensive in nature but potentially the beginning of a new regional security structure, adding that several other countries had expressed interest in joining it.

Retired Lt Gen Sikandar Afzal, retired brigadiers Nadir Mir, Imran Malik and Ghazanfar Ali, retired Air Commodore Khalid Chishti, Pildat President Ahmed Bilal Mehboob, former minister Fawad Chaudhry, Senator Ali Zafar and advocate Munir Ahmad Khan also spoke on the occasion.

Published in Dawn, September 4th, 2026

World.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs2.84, HSD by Rs2.28 per litre
World.content:
The government on Thursday raised the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.84/litre and Rs2.28/litre, respectively.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs349 per litre while HSD will cost Rs374.31 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on September 4 (Friday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Lawmakers voice concern over Wapda’s proposed ‘powers of arrest’
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Lawmakers have expressed reservations over the powers of arrest contained in the proposed Wapda Security Force (WSF) Act 2026, which could allow its personnel to detain individuals within a 1km radius of any project or installation.

During a meeting of the National Assembly Standing Committee on Water Resources, PPP members Javed Ali Shah and Saba Talpur voiced concern over the use of the ‘force’ terminology, recalling Sup­reme Court orders that forbade the creation of any new security age­n­­cy using the term ‘force’ in its name.

In response, Wapda Chairman retired Gen Muhammad Saeed told the panel the bill’s language had been discussed with provincial governments, and the ‘powers to arrest’ would only be used in case of trespass in or around a project area or installations.

He said the powers envisioned for the proposed force were in line with those afforded to the Airports Security Force (ASF) which was responsible for security within the airport jurisdictions as well as outside the premises. Such measures, he said, would be unavoidable if major infrastructure and installations were to be secured.

A legal team from the Ministry of Law told the panel that any arrest under the proposed law would follow the criminal procedure code (CrPC), and that any person arrested within a 1km radius of the project would immediately be handed over to police.

They also clarified that the apex court had barred private security agencies from using the term ‘force’, adding that the SC decision had nothing to do with state-sanctioned security agencies.

The decision to create a standalone force came in the wake of two terrorist attacks on engineers and workers of the over $6 billion Dasu Hydropower Project, in July 2021 and March 2024, which claimed the lives of several Chinese and Pakistani workers.

Initially, CPEC-related security was extended to the Dasu project, but Mr Saeed said the CPEC North and South Divisions had their own responsibilities while provinces also faced problems in providing their forces to the Wapda.

Published in Dawn, September 4th, 2026

World.title: Judge criticises Mir Raza’s business partner for concealing facts
World.content:
KARACHI: While recording testimony of victim’s business partner, the judicial commission formed to investigate the circumstances and possible negligence in the Mir Raza Ali murder case on Thursday expressed resentment towards him for attempting to mislead the commission and concealing facts about the case.

The one-member commission headed by Justice Omar Sial of the Sindh High Court grilled Muhammad Ahmed Bhardey for over two hours and deplored that he seemed to be more interested in securing his financial and business interests instead of bothering about the well-being of his childhood friend after he had gone missing.

The friend also asserted that their eatery Wafflix was doing well, but the aggrieved family was facing financial issues due to losses sustained by the victim’s father and Raza was worried since the creditors were harassing the complainant.

The commission also recorded the testimonies of Bhardey’s brother, a cab driver and a police officer.

Judicial commission records testimony in murder probe

The business partner testified that he had a personal and professional relationship with the victim and both were old friends as they had studied at school and college together.

He also deposed that they had set up the business in 2020 and on the night of July 28, he along with his elder brother Abdullah had visited the victim’s house and they along with some other friends had searched the room of Raza in order to find any clue about his whereabouts.

He further asserted that the deceased’s smart watch, keys, a packet of cigarettes along with narcotics and other articles were found in the room and the victim’s sister had helped them decode the smart watch.

When the commission asked whether he had got the partnership deed from the room, Bhardey contended that the deed was registered in 2021 and he had obtained the same from the victim in 2024 after the Sindh Board of Revenue had issued them a notice about non-registration and since then the original partnership deed had been with him as there was no copy of such document.

“I had asked the sister of victim to send a mail to Foodpanda asking it to transfer the weekly payment of their eatery (Rs600,000 to Rs800,000) to my account instead of victim on the night of July 28 while two notes were found in the smart watch of deceased one related to details of creditors and other said that the victim was looking to borrow Rs30 million.”

The bench also inquired as to why his email and phone number were being used by the victim to login to his (deceased) iCloud, Bhardey merely replied that because they were very good and old friends.

When the commission further asked him whether it was not odd that he was more concerned about payment/money shortly after his business partner and old friend had gone missing. He contended that initially, he did not take it seriously since the victim had gone missing last year as well and then returned home.

The business partner also said he came to know on July 28 morning that the pistol of a security guard, kept at one of their eatery’s branches, was missing and the footage showed the deceased was leaving the branch with the weapon and he had informed the family about such footage.

Responding to another query, he further asserted that their eatery was not facing any financial constraint, but Raza’s family was in fiscal crisis after losses in his father’s business and he was worried since people were harassing and demanding the return of the borrowed money as his parents had also sold their various assets.

“Various lenders, from whom Raza or his family borrowed money, had contacted me after Raza had gone missing while the victim had also invested two to three million rupees in the crypto trading,” he added.

Initially, Bhardey informed the commission that only he and the victim had equal partnership in the business. However, the commission had shown him a copy of another agreement which reflected that one Ahsan Anis Shamsi had also a 30 per cent partnership in the eatery.

Thereafter, he conceded the same and also added that two brothers Asif and Abid had also invested 10.5 million while he had asked Raza to keep the payment of Rs5 million made by Shamsi.

The commission expressed serious resentment towards him for not offering satisfactory replies and pointed out that he did not bother to follow up with the victim over an amount of Rs5 million, but seemed wor an amount of Rs5 million, but seemed worried about Rs600,000 shortly after his business partner had gone missing.

Justice Sial also came down hard on Bhardey for attempting to mislead the commission and conceal the facts related to the case while the commission further expressed its displeasure with his counsel for interfering in the proceedings.

When asked why he had obtained interim pre-arrest bail despite the fact that police have yet to name anybody as accused in the case, he asserted that the family of victim was pointing finger at him while the police had also detained him for 36 hours.

Abdullah Bhardey deposed that his brother and the victim owned Wafflix and he was associated as a vendor with the firm since he was supplying chocolate.

He mainly endorsed the statement of his younger brother and admitted that he was also present when the victim’s room was searched and got details about two notes found in the smart watch.

He also deposed that the victim lastly talked to him on phone at 2:30am on July 28, assured him that he (victim) will clear his payment as well as money of two other vendors.

Ehsanullah testified that he was a driver of a car, provided by ride hailing service Bykea, and had picked Raza near Khalid Bin Waleed Road at 4:09am on July 28 and dropped him at the destination in Block I, Gulistan-i-Jauhar, on 4:28am. He also said that the victim was using his mobile and also played a song during the journey, but did not talk much apart from asking the driver to speed up and take the shortest possible route.

However, he complained to the commission that the landlord has thrown him out of his rented house and ride hailing firm has also taken back the vehicle from him due to this case.

“I am jobless now and left with no option but to stay at the police station,” he added.

Thereafter, the commission issued directives to the investigating officer of the case to take such issues with the landlord and ride hailing company and addressed the same as well as to ensure that no coercive action be taken against the driver.

DSP Arshad Afridi deposed that he along with the SHO Ferozabad on the night between July 30 and July 31 had visited the house of the victim to collect information and denied that he had asked anything about possibility of suicide to the aggrieved family.

He conceded that the SHO had shown a clip to the family in which the weapon was seen in the victim’s hand.

The commission also issued a show-cause notice to MLO Dr Osama Sheikh with direction to file reply in seven days after some journalists complained that some persons accompanying the MLO at the last hearing had snatched mobile phone of one of their colleagues when he attempted to speak to the MLO on the premises of the SHC.
